meta.title: Retrieval, Generation, and Industrial Recommendation
meta.intro: This map tracks the convergence of neural information retrieval, generative search indexes, and multi-stage industrial recommendation. It traces how systems balance dense text encoders, structural hypergraphs, and long-sequence behavior representations.
meta.name: cs.IR, September 2026

papers.t: Uncertainty Quantification for LLM Agents: A Taxonomy, an Evaluation Protocol, and an Empirical Study
papers.idea: The paper surveys uncertainty quantification across the multi-step agent lifecycle. It introduces a taxonomy analyzing how uncertainty originates, propagates, and compounds during planning, tool invocation, and retrieval. An evaluation protocol and empirical experiments demonstrate how early trajectory errors compromise downstream reliability.
papers.link: Both papers tackle compound error propagation in multi-stage systems, but 2609.07395 studies uncertainty across agent planning and tool execution while UNIQUE replaces hierarchical quantization with flat quantization inside a unified recommendation engine.

papers.t: EigenLI: Spectral Approximations to Late Interaction
papers.idea: Late-interaction models represent documents with many token vectors, causing high storage and scoring costs. This paper identifies a low-rank structure in document embeddings and introduces a spectral compression method based on dominant eigendirections. It also derives a single-vector representation for approximate nearest-neighbor search from the second-order summary.
papers.link: Both papers address high-dimensional vector representations and efficiency trade-offs, but 2609.07561 derives spectral approximations to compress multi-vector late-interaction document models, whereas UNIQUE quantizes item spaces to unify retrieval and ranking.

papers.t: Open Tabular Insight Extraction: Where Do We Stand, and Where Should We Go?
papers.idea: The paper formalizes Open Tabular Insight Extraction (OpenTI) to unite fragmented research across table QA, text-to-SQL, and data analysis agents. It establishes foundational principles, taxonomies, and evaluation criteria for extracting analytical insights from large table corpora. Based on a systematic review of existing systems and benchmarks, it outlines a research agenda targeting end-to-end analytical workflows.
papers.link: Both papers target information extraction from large corpora, but 2609.07629 benchmarks text-to-SQL and table reasoning agents, whereas UNIQUE designs a unified neural architecture for large-scale industrial item recommendation.

papers.t: Noēsis: Deterministic-First Retrieval with Two-Tier Context Hydration for Factuality-Critical Queries on Small Local Models
papers.idea: Noēsis is a deterministic-first retrieval plane for small language models handling factuality-critical queries. It separates quantitative metric facts from prose through precomputed fact layers, positional alignment, and provenance routing. An initial skeleton context resolves numerical answers, while full narrative text hydrates on demand.
papers.link: Both papers optimize multi-phase context processing, but 2609.07663 separates deterministic factual extraction from narrative text hydration in RAG, whereas UNIQUE unifies candidate retrieval and CTR ranking within a single generative model.

papers.t: Cassette: Case-to-Case Structural Distillation for Efficient Legal Case Retrieval
papers.idea: Cassette addresses the inference latency of graph-based legal case retrieval. It distills structural relationships from a graph neural network teacher into a two-tower student retriever. This enables fast inference on unseen queries without dynamic graph updates.
papers.link: Both papers seek to speed up candidate retrieval, but 2609.08185 distills graph neural network structures into two-tower legal text retrievers, whereas UNIQUE relies on quantized codes to collapse retrieval and ranking into one model.

papers.t: Exploring Bottom-Up Clustering for Creating Semantic IDs
papers.idea: The paper generates unique Semantic IDs for generative retrieval via bottom-up clustering. Items are assigned to distinct leaf nodes first to guarantee uniqueness and preserve local neighborhood structure. The hierarchical codes retain embedding distance relationships while avoiding codebook collapse and collisions.
papers.link: Both papers explore semantic identifier generation to prevent codebook collapse in generative retrieval, but 2609.08310 builds hierarchical IDs through bottom-up clustering while UNIQUE replaces hierarchical IDs with single-layer flat quantization.

papers.t: SequenceO1: End-to-End Ultra-Long (100K) Sequence Modeling in Recommendation with Low-Rank Caching
papers.idea: SequenceO1 scales user behavior modeling to 100K interactions in recommendation systems. It compresses raw user history into a fixed-size sketch via prototype-based Sketch Attention and passes it alongside recent interactions to a downstream ranker. System optimizations including Multi-Request Level Batching, KV caching, pipeline lift, and FlashSA amortize and overlap sketch computation during training and inference.
papers.link: Both papers optimize industrial recommender architectures, but 2609.08443 focuses on low-rank KV caching to extend user sequence histories to 100K items, while UNIQUE unifies the retrieval and ranking phases using flat quantization.

papers.t: Individual Text Corpora Predict User-Specific Knowledge: Benchmarks of Individualized Knowledge Simulation
papers.idea: The paper investigates simulating user-specific crystallized knowledge by conditioning language models on individual web browsing histories. It uses retrieval-augmented generation over scraped search history corpora to predict participants' answers on multiple-choice general knowledge tests. The authors measure model calibration and match accuracy against individual response patterns.
papers.link: Both papers exploit user historical interaction trails, but 2609.08532 retrieves browsing history to simulate personalized test-taking behavior with language models, whereas UNIQUE directly predicts candidate item codes for feed recommendation.

papers.t: PDMR: Passage-Driven Multi-ID Document Retrieval
papers.idea: Generative retrieval models often compress an entire document into a single identifier, losing fine-grained semantic details. PDMR decomposes documents into passages and assigns multiple passage-level identifiers to provide diverse access points. A generative sequence-to-sequence model learns query-to-passage mappings and aggregates passage scores for document ranking.
papers.link: Both papers deploy generative retrieval over learned identifiers, but 2609.08762 maps queries to multiple passage-level IDs for text ranking, whereas UNIQUE uses single-layer flat quantization to unify retrieval and ranking in item feeds.

papers.t: REDSI: Addressing the Reproducibility and Evaluation Consistency of Differentiable Search Indexing for Document Retrieval
papers.idea: The paper provides an open-source reproduction framework for Differentiable Search Indexing that supports atomic, naive, and semantic document identifiers. It establishes a standardized reconstruction pipeline for the NQ320K dataset to eliminate preprocessing inconsistencies across benchmarks. Experiments evaluate retrieval effectiveness and parameter efficiency under downscaled model configurations.
papers.link: Both papers focus on identifier construction in generative retrieval, but 2609.08860 benchmarks standard atomic and semantic document IDs on NQ320K, whereas UNIQUE introduces feedback-aware flat quantization to represent long-tail items in recommendation.

papers.t: Q2D-Web: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Retrieval in Agentic RAG Systems
papers.idea: Q2D-Web evaluates first-stage retrievers on machine-reformulated queries from production agentic search. It pairs a 190M-document web corpus with roughly 70k queries across ten languages, incorporating relevance judgments from agent citations, production rankings, and pooled LLM annotations. Subcorpus sampling via reciprocal rank fusion reduces corpus size while preserving comparative retriever rankings.
papers.link: Both papers evaluate first-stage retrieval over massive candidate sets, but 2609.08887 constructs a web benchmark for agentic query reformulations, whereas UNIQUE unifies candidate generation with downstream ranking for recommender feeds.

papers.t: FINALLY: A Dataset Recommender System for Recommender-Systems Research
papers.idea: FINALLY is a web-based recommender system that selects benchmark dataset sets for offline recommender-system evaluations. Users configure target-set sizes, metadata filters, candidate restrictions, and required datasets. The system selects collections using random, diverse, and non-diverse strategies based on adapted Effective Covariance and Convex Hull objectives.
papers.link: Both papers target recommendation research, but 2609.08941 recommends evaluation benchmark datasets to researchers, whereas UNIQUE proposes an operational neural architecture unifying retrieval and ranking in industrial feeds.

papers.t: Extracting Semantics from Cattle Reporting Categories for Data Interoperability and Findability
papers.idea: Livestock data across national and international sources lack standardized descriptions. The authors extract and normalize cattle reporting terms from heterogeneous agricultural census and survey datasets. They compare extracted concepts against standard vocabularies like AGROVOC to evaluate semantic interoperability.
papers.link: Both papers handle domain categorization, but 2609.09381 harmonizes agricultural survey terms to standard ontologies, whereas UNIQUE designs quantized semantic identifiers for candidate retrieval in web feeds.

papers.t: Should I Be Polite to My LLM Relevance Judge? Tone as a Severity Operating-Point Shift
papers.idea: This paper analyzes the effect of prompt tone on LLM relevance judges across multiple models and calibrated politeness levels. The authors propose an operating-point account where tone alters judge severity and leniency rather than discriminative ability. Prompt tone shifts absolute calibration metrics like Cohen's kappa while largely preserving ranking order.
papers.link: Both papers investigate ranking evaluation, but 2609.09703 evaluates prompt tone effects on LLM relevance judges, whereas UNIQUE focuses on training an end-to-end quantized model for feed retrieval and scoring.

papers.t: Purchase Advice and Observable Buyer Responses in Real AI Conversations
papers.idea: This paper audits real AI conversation logs to measure purchase advice and observable buyer responses. The authors screen historical assistant interactions for purchase missions and inspect subsequent user messages. They show that while assistants frequently supply product options, recorded user responses almost never contain explicit purchase commitments or abandonment decisions.
papers.link: Both papers study commercial item recommendations, but 2609.09878 audits real-world conversational AI dialogues for buyer commitment signals, whereas UNIQUE designs an industrial system architecture for automated feed recommendation.

papers.t: Guaranteeing Faithful Evidence Extraction in Speculative Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.idea: Standard retrieval-augmented generation relies on probabilistic decoding and can introduce hallucinations into answers. This paper introduces a speculative retrieval-augmented generation framework to guarantee verbatim evidence extraction from supporting documents. The approach couples generative models with exact text spans to ensure compliance in safety-critical applications.
papers.link: Both papers alter generative decoding to improve reliability, but 2609.10046 enforces verbatim passage extraction for factual RAG, whereas UNIQUE predicts quantized codes for candidate retrieval followed by discriminative scoring.

papers.t: LiteRAG: Cost-Efficient Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.idea: LiteRAG removes LLM calls from query-time graph retrieval. It selects semantic and lexical anchors, expands subgraphs with dynamic thresholds and community hub penalties, and formats the result into compact reasoning chains for generation.
papers.link: Both papers optimize multi-stage retrieval workflows, but 2609.10239 eliminates LLM calls via graph path traversal for multi-hop QA, whereas UNIQUE replaces the multi-stage recommender funnel with a single quantized model.

papers.t: When Synthetic Data Hurts: On Catastrophic Forgetting in Skill Retrieval for LLM Agents
papers.idea: Fine-tuning dense retrievers and rerankers on synthetic data improves in-distribution skill selection for LLM agents but causes catastrophic forgetting on real tasks. Regularization techniques from continual learning prevent this degradation across bi-encoders and cross-encoders. These methods preserve out-of-distribution skill retrieval while enhancing in-distribution synthetic accuracy.
papers.link: Both papers train dense neural candidate selectors, but 2609.10750 mitigates catastrophic forgetting during skill retrieval fine-tuning, whereas UNIQUE unifies generative code retrieval with discriminative CTR ranking.

papers.t: UniRec: Cross-stage Multi-Task Fusion with Preference Alignment for Cascaded Recommender Systems
papers.idea: Cascaded recommender systems suffer from preference mismatches between pre-ranking and ranking stages. UniRec jointly optimizes multi-task fusion across stages using a coupled dual-agent architecture. It introduces dual-axis preference alignment and attribute group-relative regularization to reconcile cross-stage objectives without amplifying attribute-dependent bias.
papers.link: Both papers resolve misalignment between pre-ranking and ranking stages, but 2609.11052 couples them via dual-agent preference alignment, whereas UNIQUE collapses both stages into a single unified quantization model.

papers.t: VikingRAG: Accurate and Token-efficient Retrieval-augmented Generation over Structured Documents
papers.idea: VikingRAG organizes structured documents into a hierarchical semantic storage model for retrieval-augmented generation. It closes the feedback loop between evidence retrieval and reasoning through evidence-gap-driven multi-round search. Query-adaptive experience edges and escalation mechanisms refine subsequent traversals across document trees.
papers.link: Both papers address retrieval over hierarchical data structures, but 2609.11390 navigates structured document trees for RAG, whereas UNIQUE replaces hierarchical semantic codes with flat quantization to prevent error propagation.

papers.t: TimelyRAG: Semantic-Temporal Hybrid Retrieval for Time-Critical Question Answering in Overlapping-Evolving Documents
papers.idea: TimelyRAG performs temporal reranking on candidate documents for retrieval-augmented generation in overlapping-evolving corpora like laws and regulations. It computes semantic similarity first, then re-ranks candidate versions using temporal distance between query validity targets and clause-level validity periods.
papers.link: Both papers improve multi-stage candidate scoring, but 2609.11572 reranks temporal documents using validity windows for question answering, whereas UNIQUE performs target-code-aware discriminative scoring for feed ranking.

papers.t: FedHUR: Learning Hierarchical Utility-Guided Client Relations for Personalized Federated Recommendation
papers.idea: FedHUR enables personalized federated recommendation by modeling hierarchical client relationships and assessing client utility. The system mines multi-granularity relations across clients and retrieves useful client updates. Clients then aggregate model parameters with personalized filtering before local fine-tuning.
papers.link: Both papers address recommender modeling, but 2609.11632 focuses on privacy-preserving client parameter aggregation in federated settings, whereas UNIQUE develops a centralized unified retrieval-ranking architecture.

papers.t: Your Retriever Already Knows: Distribution-Shape QPP for RAG Retrieval Sufficiency
papers.idea: Predicting retrieval sufficiency in RAG pipelines prevents generation hallucinations without ground-truth labels. The method extracts non-lexical score-distribution, query-surface, and global features from retriever outputs to classify whether top documents contain the answer. These features outperform local LLM judges at low latency and can combine with them in hybrid setups.
papers.link: Both papers deal with candidate scoring reliability, but 2609.11646 uses retriever score distributions to predict answer presence in RAG, whereas UNIQUE integrates candidate retrieval and CTR scoring within one model.

papers.t: Generative Late-Interaction Embeddings For Visual Document Retrieval
papers.idea: Late-interaction visual document retrieval stores large sets of patch embeddings per page. This paper compresses the representation by projecting per-page cluster centroids onto the unit sphere and learning a compact code. A lightweight decoder expands these compressed vectors back into the full set at query time for candidate rescoring.
papers.link: Both papers apply vector quantization to candidate representations, but 2609.11808 quantizes visual page centroids for late-interaction document search, whereas UNIQUE quantizes item embeddings into single-layer codes for feed recommendation.

papers.t: Recommendation Retrievers Need Verifiers: Universal Generative Reranking for Sequential Recommendations
papers.idea: First-stage recommenders retrieve a candidate pool, but only a short prefix is passed downstream. This method keeps the retriever frozen as a drafter and trains a lightweight generative verifier using next-token cross-entropy. The verifier scores candidate identifier tokens conditioned on the retriever state, and reciprocal rank fusion reranks the candidate pool.
papers.link: Both papers integrate generative modeling into sequential recommendation, but 2609.12270 maintains a separate retriever and verifier reranker, whereas UNIQUE unites retrieval and ranking into a single model.

papers.t: ChronicleRec: Pre-training Temporally Anchored Tokens for Lifelong User Modeling
papers.idea: ChronicleRec models lifelong user behavior sequences through temporally anchored summary tokens. It applies recency-aware sequence merging, causal query-token interleaving, and multi-horizon compression to decouple long-history encoding from candidate scoring. Downstream rankers cache and reuse target-independent chronicle representations for low-latency scoring.
papers.link: Both papers target industrial recommendation latency, but 2609.12375 compresses lifelong sequence histories into reusable chronicle tokens, whereas UNIQUE compresses item representations via flat quantization to collapse the retrieval-ranking funnel.

papers.t: Preference-Drift-Aware Subsequence Learning and Hierarchical Context Fusion for Long-Sequence Generative Recommendation
papers.idea: This paper presents a framework for long-sequence generative recommendation that addresses computational cost and preference drift. It detects soft subsequence boundaries using multidimensional drift signals and aggregates items via linear attention. Cross-attention connects recent interactions with relevant subsequence contexts, followed by gated fusion to output a target representation encoding both recent and long-term preferences.
papers.link: Both papers deploy semantic identifiers for generative recommendation, but 2609.12556 models long sequence drift with attention across item subsequences, whereas UNIQUE focuses on flat quantization to unify retrieval with ranking.

papers.t: Personalized and Trust-Aware Health Recommendation Policies for a Construction Workplace
papers.idea: The paper models interactions between construction workers and a health recommender system as a Markov Decision Process. Worker health and trust evolve dynamically, influencing compliance with interventions. Recommender policies balance health, productivity, and trust using short-horizon control and reinforcement learning.
papers.link: Both papers model sequential recommendation decisions, but 2609.12679 implements an MDP for workplace safety interventions, whereas UNIQUE optimizes large-scale web feed systems through end-to-end vector quantization.

papers.t: Learning the Lake: Reliable Experience for Adaptive Data Product Discovery
papers.idea: SafeLake introduces Evolving Discovery Memory to avoid repeated full-lake searches in data-product discovery. Operational familiarity controls search scope, product evidence routes retrieval across a regional index, and audit mechanisms provide fallback for adaptive queries.
papers.link: Both papers improve candidate search over vast pools, but 2609.12754 manages scoped memory indices for tabular data lakes, whereas UNIQUE applies flat quantization and generative code prediction to web feed recommendation.

papers.t: A Historical Corpus Is Not a Historical System: Auditing Hindsight Leakage in Stateful Data Discovery
papers.idea: Historical offline evaluations often leak future interaction memory into retrieval replays even when candidate corpora are frozen. PIT Discovery aligns frozen corpus snapshots with point-in-time interaction memory strictly preceding each query anchor. This counterfactual framework isolates hindsight leakage and measures hindsight gain in stateful retrieval systems.
papers.link: Both papers consider sequential user interaction data, but 2609.12766 establishes auditing protocols against hindsight leakage in stateful retrieval, whereas UNIQUE designs a model unifying candidate retrieval and ranking.

papers.t: MIMA: Multi-Interest Recommendation via Multi-Positive Exclusive Assignment
papers.idea: Multi-interest recommender models often suffer from interest collapse under single-positive training. MIMA introduces a multi-positive exclusive assignment framework to mitigate this issue. It uses multi-positive targets, a causal decoder to generate complementary interest vectors, and exclusive assignment during training to enforce distinct specialization across user interests.
papers.link: Both papers improve candidate selection in recommender systems, but 2609.12842 trains multi-interest vectors using exclusive assignment, whereas UNIQUE bypasses multi-vector matching by predicting discrete quantized codes directly.

papers.t: Decoupling Error Attribution in Cloud-Native Graph-RAG: A Data Integrity Diagnostic Framework
papers.idea: A diagnostic framework decomposes Graph-RAG pipeline errors into reasoning loss, knowledge graph defects, and query generation failures. It injects controlled data perturbations into a spatio-temporal ecological knowledge graph. The analysis shows graph structural defects dominate performance degradation while parametric memory masks retrieval breakdowns.
papers.link: Both papers analyze architectural failures across retrieval steps, but 2609.13324 isolates structural errors in graph RAG systems, whereas UNIQUE addresses error propagation in recommendation by replacing hierarchical codes with flat quantization.

papers.t: PCGNet: Unifying Shared and Specific Information for Fashion Matching Recommendations
papers.idea: PCGNet recommends fashion item pairs by balancing user personalization and item compatibility. The architecture refines graph representations and uses mutual information objectives to capture both shared and view-specific signals across users and items.
papers.link: Both papers optimize personalized item recommendations, but 2609.13339 uses graph neural networks and mutual information for fashion compatibility, whereas UNIQUE applies vector quantization to unify general feed retrieval and ranking.

papers.t: Mixture-of-Experts Language Models Can Be Strong and Efficient Retrievers
papers.idea: Mixture-of-Experts language models serve as first-stage dense retrievers by encoding queries and passages using a subset of activated parameters. Fine-tuning MoE backbones via LoRA yields retrieval accuracy competitive with larger dense models while lowering query latency. Routing queries through fewer active experts at test time preserves ranking performance without retraining.
papers.link: Both papers optimize dense retrieval efficiency, but 2609.13486 activates sparse expert subnetworks within text bi-encoders, whereas UNIQUE quantizes item representations to generate candidate codes sequentially.

papers.t: Pre-retrieval Query Clustering for Adaptive Top-k Document Retrieval in RAG Systems
papers.idea: Standard RAG pipelines retrieve a fixed number of documents regardless of query difficulty. This paper introduces QCAR, which predicts optimal retrieval depth before search by clustering query embeddings offline and assigning depth thresholds per cluster. Online inference assigns incoming queries to clusters to dynamically determine top-k document retrieval.
papers.link: Both papers adapt candidate retrieval boundaries, but 2609.13489 clusters queries offline to dynamically determine retrieval depth for RAG, whereas UNIQUE predicts quantized item tokens directly to unify retrieval with ranking.

papers.t: Addressing Cross-Stage Decoupling of Semantic and Collaborative Signals in Generative Recommendation
papers.idea: Two-stage generative recommendation models decouple semantic item tokens from collaborative interaction patterns. This framework supplements collaborative signals into tokenization and fuses textual semantics during autoregressive generation. Hyperbolic manifold alignment bridges discrete token embeddings and continuous language model representations.
papers.link: Both papers combine semantic item tokens with collaborative signals in generative recommendation, but 2609.13678 bridges them via hyperbolic alignment, while UNIQUE uses feedback-aware flat quantization to prevent hierarchical error propagation.

papers.t: Odds-Shift Slippage in One-vs-Rest Rankers: Diagnosing and Repairing Reweighting-Induced Top-K Errors
papers.idea: Per-label positive-class weights in one-vs-rest models alter row-level top-K rankings by shifting odds unevenly across labels. Finite learners encounter slippage through leaf-step caps or saturated score ties. The paper formalizes this degradation and evaluates analytic inversion alongside per-label calibration to repair the rankings.
papers.link: Both papers tackle ranking calibration issues under class imbalance, but 2609.13810 repairs top-K odds-shift slippage in one-vs-rest classifiers, whereas UNIQUE applies target-code-aware discriminative scoring inside a generative quantization framework.

papers.t: P$^3$Rec: Distilling Prior--Posterior Preference Reasoning for LLM-based Recommendation
papers.idea: P3Rec extracts target-agnostic prior preferences and target-conditioned posterior preferences from large language models to train lightweight recommender systems. It internalizes both perspectives through dual representation alignment and adapts them during inference via preference retrieval. This setup allows efficient deployment without online LLM querying.
papers.link: Both papers improve sequential recommendation scoring, but 2609.13993 distills prior and posterior LLM preferences into lightweight representations, whereas UNIQUE couples generative retrieval and discriminative ranking via flat quantization.

papers.t: VARG: Value-Aware and Ranking-Aligned Generative Retrieval for Dynamic E-commerce Search
papers.idea: VARG is an e-commerce generative retrieval system that feeds candidate items directly to the final ranker, bypassing pre-ranking. It uses semantic prefixes from RQ-VAE combined with value-ordered tokens for item identifiers, trained through three-stage supervised fine-tuning and prefix-aware reinforcement learning.
papers.link: Both papers replace the conventional recommendation funnel with generative retrieval, but 2609.14493 uses hierarchical RQ-VAE prefixes combined with value tokens, whereas UNIQUE rejects hierarchical quantization in favor of feedback-aware flat quantization.

papers.t: The Wisdom of the Loudest: A Large-Scale Audit of Generative Search on Reddit
papers.idea: This paper audits Reddit Answers, an AI-mediated platform search engine. The authors analyze how generative search samples communities, filters user comments, and alters conversational tone across runs.
papers.link: Both papers examine generative information discovery platforms, but 2609.14575 conducts an empirical audit of community sourcing in Reddit Answers, whereas UNIQUE builds an internal architecture for feed recommendation.

papers.t: Beyond Benchmark Scores: How Synthetic and Authentic Query Distributions Diverge in RAG Evaluation
papers.idea: The paper analyzes how synthetic and authentic user queries diverge during RAG evaluation. It compares synthetic question-answer pairs against genuine student queries in an administrative chatbot case study across query length, intent, source coverage, and retrieval behavior. Results show that retrieval setups optimized for synthetic queries drop in performance on authentic user traffic.
papers.link: Both papers study industrial system behavior under real user distributions, but 2609.14579 measures performance gaps between authentic and synthetic queries in RAG, whereas UNIQUE constructs a feed recommender evaluated on production logs.

papers.t: EviQE: Evidence Selection for LLM-Based Query Expansion
papers.idea: EviQE treats query expansion as a document selection problem prior to text generation. It executes multiple query reformulators independently, aggregates the retrieved candidates into a single pool, and selects a compact set of informative passages. An LLM then generates grounded expansion text from these selected documents.
papers.link: Both papers combine retrieval and scoring stages, but 2609.14875 selects retrieved evidence passages to feed into LLM query expanders, whereas UNIQUE performs candidate retrieval and ranking within a single quantized neural framework.

papers.t: Route Me If You Can: A Benchmark for Query Reformulation Selection
papers.idea: QueryRoute benchmarks query reformulation selection for information retrieval. It freezes candidate query pools generated by multiple LLM backbones across diverse datasets and retrievers. Selectors choose a single reformulation per query without test relevance labels to evaluate per-query routing performance.
papers.link: Both papers optimize first-stage retrieval pipelines, but 2609.14885 benchmarks model routing for query reformulation, whereas UNIQUE integrates retrieval and ranking via single-layer quantized item representations.

papers.t: LazFormer: Scaling Transformers for Industrial Recommendation via Transferable Generative Pre-training
papers.idea: LazFormer scales Transformers for industrial recommendation using a pre-training and ranking paradigm. It pairs generative sequence pre-training with a transferable residual adapter to inject ranking-specific features without disrupting pre-trained representations, using asymmetric multi-epoch training to mitigate sparse parameter overfitting.
papers.link: Both papers scale Transformers for industrial recommendation, but 2609.14978 focuses on generative pre-training with residual ranking adapters, whereas UNIQUE combines generative code retrieval with discriminative scoring into one quantized model.

papers.t: Generate to Explore, Select to Exploit: Aligning LLM-based Headline Generation with Personalized Recommendation
papers.idea: GESE decouples personalized headline generation into exploration and exploitation stages. A large language model generates a diverse candidate pool of headlines using policy optimization with hierarchical rewards. A lightweight selector then uses real-time feedback signals to pick the headline matching the user context.
papers.link: Both papers separate item exploration from precise ranking, but 2609.15094 generates textual headline variants with an LLM before selection, whereas UNIQUE predicts quantized item identifiers and scores them discriminatively.

papers.t: Top-K Is Not a Budget for Hybrid Retrieval
papers.idea: DiBud runs hybrid retrieval under an explicit list-access budget rather than a fixed cutoff depth or output count. It maintains upper and lower bounds on unread ranks to incrementally certify the exact reciprocal rank fusion prefix. Selective list reading resolves candidate competitions until the access budget stops execution.
papers.link: Both papers optimize candidate list selection, but 2609.15143 provides budgeted rank fusion algorithms for text retrievers, whereas UNIQUE relies on target-code-aware discriminative scoring within a single-stage model.

papers.t: ProLiVis 2.0: Literature-Centric Visualization of Protein--Protein Interaction Networks, with a Citation-Trust Model for Interaction Evidence
papers.idea: ProLiVis 2.0 visualizes protein-protein interaction networks alongside literature evidence directly in the browser. It scores interaction reliability using a seven-term citation-trust model that tracks independent laboratory affiliations. A deterministic O(n log n) layout replaces force-directed algorithms to ensure reproducible visualizations.
papers.link: Both papers handle large entity networks, but 2609.15236 constructs browser visualizations for protein interactions and citation trust, whereas UNIQUE designs an industrial neural architecture for personalized feed recommendation.

papers.t: Clean Scores, Buried Evidence, and Confident Wrong: A Receipt-Based Audit of Frontier Agentic QA
papers.idea: This paper audits frontier LLM agents in a financial due diligence setting with clean versus buried evidence conditions. When target evidence sits among noise, agents suffer drops in accuracy, call more tools, and pair correct numeric tables with fabricated explanations. The authors argue for statement-level receipts and adversarial auditing instead of leaderboard confidence scores.
papers.link: Both papers identify reliability failures in multi-step AI systems, but 2609.15319 audits LLM agent hallucinations in financial question answering, whereas UNIQUE addresses candidate error propagation in recommender systems.

papers.t: Benchmarking Embedding Models for ESG Data
papers.idea: The paper constructs a benchmark dataset tailored to Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) documents. It evaluates fourteen open-source and closed-source embedding models across information retrieval and retrieval-augmented generation tasks. The results show performance variations, with Qwen-based models achieving the highest scores.
papers.link: Both papers involve dense embedding representations, but 2609.15434 benchmarks text embedding models on ESG domain retrieval, whereas UNIQUE learns quantized item representations for unified retrieval and ranking in feeds.

papers.t: The Magnitude Mirage: Rethinking Confidence for Reasoning-Intensive Retrieval
papers.idea: Retrieval-augmented generation pipelines often use raw similarity score thresholds to decide when to abstain from answering. This paper shows that raw score magnitude fails on reasoning-intensive retrieval tasks where constraint-violating documents still score high on semantic similarity. Replacing absolute score thresholds with zero-cost score-distribution signals restores retrieval abstention accuracy without additional model calls.
papers.link: Both papers address scoring signals in retrieval architectures, but 2609.15578 uses score distribution shapes to trigger abstention in RAG, whereas UNIQUE feeds target-code-aware discriminative scores to rank feed candidates.

papers.t: Self-Evolving Memory for Generative Recommendation
papers.idea: Continual adaptation in generative recommenders causes dominant patterns to overpower underrepresented ones in a shared parameter space. The authors introduce a self-evolving memory framework that isolates behavioral patterns using a sparse Key-Value memory layer. A consolidation loss reinforces the learning of underrepresented dynamics during continual training.
papers.link: Both papers address sequential patterns in generative recommender systems. UNIQUE replaces multi-stage pipelines with unified quantization-based prediction, whereas this paper uses key-value memory to prevent underrepresented patterns from being overwritten during continual adaptation.

papers.t: IROH: Insightful Ranking Of Humor using Multi-Stage Hybrid Retrieval with Rationale-Distilled LLM Judges for JOKER 2026 Track Task 1 English
papers.idea: IROH ranks humorous texts using a three-stage retrieval pipeline. It combines hybrid BM25 and dense retrieval with cross-encoder reranking and an ensemble of LoRA-adapted language model judges. The judges evaluate candidates using query-aware rationales generated during training.
papers.link: Both works tackle multi-stage candidate scoring pipelines. UNIQUE collapses retrieval and ranking into a single unified framework, whereas IROH keeps a classic decoupled pipeline combining BM25, dense retrieval, and LLM judges.

papers.t: Evaluating Brand Retrieval and Ranking in Large Language Model Recommendations
papers.idea: This paper presents a framework to measure and diagnose brand recommendations generated by large language models. The method evaluates prevalence and prominence metrics, such as Brand Recommendation Probability and Mean Reciprocal Rank, against independently defined competitive sets. It analyzes how prompt specificity and stated consumer needs alter brand visibility and ranking order.
papers.link: Both studies examine item ranking in generative models. UNIQUE builds an industrial recommendation architecture using vector quantization, while this paper provides an offline evaluation protocol to audit brand exposure in commercial generative models.

papers.t: Where Post-Training Quantization Breaks Text Embedders: A Measured Map Across Four Embedder Families
papers.idea: The authors test post-training quantization rules on text embedders across four model families. They measure performance changes over varied bit widths, group sizes, and model modules. The results show that mixed-precision allocation yields minimal gain at INT4, while module sensitivity at INT3 and INT2 varies strongly by architecture family.
papers.link: Both works deal with quantization in retrieval architectures. UNIQUE uses learnable feedback-aware vector quantization to create discrete item codes, whereas this paper audits post-training weight quantization to compress continuous text embedders.

papers.t: Balancing Trial and Reorder: A Hybrid Sequential Transformer-GBDT Ranker for On-Demand Delivery
papers.idea: The paper introduces Universal Venue Ranker, a ranking system for on-demand delivery platforms. It combines a bidirectional transformer encoder for sequential purchase history modeling with a gradient-boosted decision-tree ranker. The system balances trial and reorder behavior across multiple delivery verticals using session-level multi-objective weighting.
papers.link: Both methods rank candidates in large-scale sequential recommendation feeds. UNIQUE unifies candidate generation and scoring into a single quantized transformer, whereas this paper maintains a decoupled sequential transformer followed by a GBDT ranker.

papers.t: PCap: Personalized Retrieval-Stage Diversity Capping in Facebook Marketplace
papers.idea: PCap diversifies recommendations at the retrieval stage rather than the ranking stage. It models user-level diversity preferences and applies personalized caps to candidates across content groups at the indexer-shard and aggregation levels. An automated parameter tuning sequence optimizes the high-dimensional personalized capping settings in production.
papers.link: Both focus on candidate retrieval stages in production recommender systems. UNIQUE directly optimizes item codes for joint retrieval and ranking, whereas PCap adjusts candidate diversity across distributed index shards using hard capacity limits.

papers.t: Predicting Partial Answer Quality and Utility in Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.idea: The paper investigates intermediate answer trajectories in agentic retrieval-augmented generation. It probes models at each reasoning and retrieval step to predict partial answer quality and utility gains. These predictions then guide early stopping to eliminate redundant search iterations.
papers.link: Both investigate iterative steps in generative search. UNIQUE models user feed recommendations via code generation and discriminative ranking, whereas this paper monitors intermediate reasoning steps to trigger early stopping in multi-hop question answering.

papers.t: ReliGRec: Reliability-Oriented LLM-Based Generative Recommendation via User-Risk-Aware Prompt Routing
papers.idea: ReliGRec adapts LLM-based generative recommendation to noisy or unstable user behavior. A dual-view estimator combines sequential behavior and temporal graph context to predict a user-level weak-risk score. This score routes inference between a standard prompt and a cautious prompt that emphasizes collaborative support over isolated interactions.
papers.link: Both employ semantic identifiers for generative recommendation. UNIQUE abandons hierarchical tree quantization in favor of single-layer flat codes, whereas ReliGRec uses hierarchical identifiers alongside dynamic prompt routing to handle uncertain user behavior.

papers.t: Measuring Decision-Scale Use in Tool-Augmented LLMs: A Contrastive Urban Benchmark
papers.idea: The paper introduces a benchmark to evaluate whether tool-augmented language models judge urban activity anomalies relative to local historical baselines rather than raw counts. It pairs mobility situations across three cities and tests six models under five tool-output formats. Results show models rely heavily on raw counts unless explicit baseline scores are provided in the tool output.
papers.link: Both evaluate decision accuracy in machine learning systems. UNIQUE targets high-throughput feed recommendations via quantization, whereas this paper designs an evaluation benchmark for tool-augmented agents analyzing urban anomaly data.

papers.t: AURA: Agentic Diagnosis and Refinement for Production Recommender Systems at Scale
papers.idea: AURA uses specialized LLM agents to detect qualitative failures in production recommender systems. The agents examine user interaction logs to diagnose recommendation issues, generate hypotheses, and propose code-level modifications to the recommender pipeline.
papers.link: Both address industrial recommender pipelines. UNIQUE redesigns the serving architecture to unify retrieval and ranking, while AURA introduces an agentic offline framework to diagnose bugs and suggest pipeline improvements from system logs.

papers.t: Efficient Swing Computation for Retrieval in Large-Scale Recommender Systems
papers.idea: The paper speeds up Swing similarity computation for item-to-item retrieval on bipartite graphs. It presents ASC, which uses user subset sampling and grouped sampling to approximate Swing similarities. It also introduces K-ASC to retrieve top-K items via greedy candidate generation and adaptive pairwise refinement.
papers.link: Both optimize candidate retrieval efficiency in large-scale recommender systems. UNIQUE uses generative code prediction over discrete item tokens, whereas this work accelerates graph-based Swing similarity calculations over user-item interaction matrices.

papers.t: Scaling Articulated Rationales for MLLM-based Recommendation
papers.idea: SARA converts sparse user preference explanations into recommendation signals. The system collects questionnaire feedback, trains a multimodal LLM with supervised fine-tuning and direct preference optimization to generate positive and negative rationales, and integrates the resulting text embeddings into ranking models.
papers.link: Both study multi-stage industrial ranking systems. UNIQUE derives item representations from behavioral feedback and quantization, while SARA generates textual rationales using multimodal language models to augment downstream ranking features.

papers.t: One Size Does Not Fit All! Dynamic Retriever and Generator Selection for RAG
papers.idea: Retrieval-augmented generation pipelines often waste compute by applying uniform models across varied inputs. This work introduces DRAG, a framework that dynamically routes each query to an appropriate retriever and generator pair based on predicted query difficulty. Routing uses either query performance prediction features or supervised fine-tuning.
papers.link: Both works manage retriever-generator interactions. UNIQUE merges candidate retrieval and scoring inside a single quantised feed recommender, whereas DRAG selects between distinct external sparse and dense retrievers based on query difficulty.

papers.t: DUPAR: Dual-Path Conversational Retrieval via Speech Retriever with Cross-Turn Evidence Caching
papers.idea: DUPAR performs conversational passage retrieval directly from speech queries using dual execution paths. A fast path encodes speech directly to search a cross-turn evidence cache built from prior turns and relation graph expansion. If cache confidence is low, a slow path runs automatic speech recognition and fuses full-index audio and text retrieval.
papers.link: Both propose specialized multi-path architectures for item retrieval. UNIQUE pairs generative code retrieval with discriminative ranking for feeds, whereas DUPAR builds a dual-path conversational system for caching and retrieving speech passages.

papers.t: PageRecall: Measuring Page Selection in Literature-Grounded Question Answering
papers.idea: The paper investigates evidence grounding in literature-grounded question answering on the LitTraceQA benchmark. It finds that evidence citation failures stem from page retrieval rather than reading comprehension. The system bypasses passage selection by feeding whole parsed documents into the reader model context, supplemented by structural bibliography parsing.
papers.link: Both analyze the candidate retrieval stage in retrieval pipelines. UNIQUE targets large-scale item feeds via flat quantization, whereas PageRecall examines passage selection errors in document question-answering over academic literature.

papers.t: Single-Token Expected-Value Scoring for Cold-Start Candidate Ranking
papers.idea: The paper presents a candidate ranking method for cold-start recruitment using small language models. It casts candidate-job matching as ordinal classification over numerical grades and computes relevance as the mathematical expectation of the first-token logits. A hybrid loss combining mean squared error and cross-entropy trains the model without interaction logs.
papers.link: Both optimize candidate ranking without relying exclusively on multi-layer cross-encoders. UNIQUE combines generative retrieval with target-code discriminative scoring, while this paper ranks job candidates using expected-value scoring computed over first-token logits.

papers.t: Quanta: A Self-Contained Python Library for Hybrid Retrieval over Quantised Embeddings, Lexical Indexes, and Knowledge Graphs
papers.idea: Quanta is a self-contained Python library for hybrid retrieval that integrates quantised vector search, BM25, and knowledge graph traversal. The graph acts as a candidate expander rather than a relevance scorer, admitting candidates that are re-scored by dense indexes. Output rankings are fused via weighted reciprocal rank fusion without external services.
papers.link: Both leverage quantized vectors for candidate search. UNIQUE trains an end-to-end flat quantization scheme for feed recommendation, whereas Quanta provides a Python library combining frozen quantized embeddings with BM25 and knowledge graphs.

papers.t: One-Step Retrieval Framework for Real-Time Sponsored Search Ads Using Hierarchical Text Representations
papers.idea: The paper presents a one-step generative ad retrieval framework that replaces multi-stage cascading pipelines and discrete semantic identifiers. It represents advertisements with hierarchical natural text consisting of high-level commercial intents and fine-grained ad abstracts. A single large language model performs candidate generation, relevance estimation, and ranking directly.
papers.link: Both abandon conventional multi-stage retrieval pipelines in favor of unified end-to-end architectures. UNIQUE quantizes item spaces into single-layer discrete codes, whereas this paper represents search ads using hierarchical natural language tokens.

papers.t: Exploring LLMs and RAG for Plausible and Explainable Material Prediction of Vehicle Components
papers.idea: This paper evaluates whether large language models can predict and explain plausible materials for vehicle components without fine-tuning. It compares direct generation against single-pass retrieval-augmented generation and iterative Chain-of-Verification over a domain-filtered Wikipedia corpus. Domain experts evaluate prediction quality using a custom web interface.
papers.link: Both explore retrieval-based ranking systems. UNIQUE focuses on real-time item feeds using compact quantized codes, whereas this work tests retrieval-augmented generation to predict physical material properties from domain texts.

papers.t: SURF: Subtractive Updates for Recommender Forgetting
papers.idea: SURF performs machine unlearning for sequential recommender systems by combining partition-based and influence-based approaches. The method removes the impact of deleted user-item interactions through subtractive updates. It maintains recommendation ranking stability while avoiding full model retraining.
papers.link: Both study sequential recommender systems. UNIQUE focuses on unified model architecture and quantization, whereas SURF develops subtractive parameter updates to enable machine unlearning without full model retraining.

papers.t: Beyond Similarity through Zero-Token Geometric Graphs for Multi-Hop RAG
papers.idea: Geometric Gain Graph RAG constructs a document graph without LLM extraction calls. It weights edges using directional consistency and orthogonality between document embeddings, applies a topological degree penalty, and expands query seeds via controlled diffusion to retrieve complementary evidence.
papers.link: Both address candidate retrieval over large catalogs. UNIQUE unifies candidate selection into a single quantized recommendation model, whereas this paper builds geometric passage graphs for multi-hop evidence retrieval in question answering.

papers.t: Self-Evolving Search Index
papers.idea: Self-Index enables retrieval indexes to self-evolve without human intervention. An optimizer diagnoses retrieval shortfalls, modifies responsible index keys, and validates updates before writing them. A query simulator creates hypothetical queries to explore additional retrieval demands.
papers.link: Both modify the indexing mechanism of retrieval systems. UNIQUE optimizes single-layer flat codes end-to-end with the model, whereas Self-Index uses automated agentic loops to alter sparse and dense index keys based on query performance.

papers.t: Dense Feature Representation over Sequence Modeling: A Solution to the KDD Cup 2026 UniRec Challenge
papers.idea: The authors analyze conversion-rate prediction backbones on the KDD Cup 2026 UniRec dataset using leaderboard ablations. They improve a baseline model through dense feature preprocessing, merged single-stream sequence modeling, and orthogonalized optimization. Empirical results show that dense feature transformations drive most performance gains, whereas sequence modeling variations offer minimal improvements.
papers.link: Both target large-scale click and conversion rate prediction tasks. UNIQUE modifies the model architecture to integrate generative retrieval and ranking, whereas this paper studies input feature preprocessing and sequence backbones for standard tubular pipelines.

papers.t: Reproducing Transparent and Scrutable Recommendations: Exploring Open-Weight Models via Natural-Language User Profiles
papers.idea: This paper reproduces and evaluates User Profile Recommendation, which summarizes user reviews into natural-language profiles for recommendation scoring. The authors test context ablations and multi-seed stability across open-weight models. Mechanistic interpretability analysis with activation steering reveals that profile perturbations shift ratings uniformly rather than altering item rankings.
papers.link: Both focus on candidate ranking algorithms. UNIQUE designs an industrial unified recommender using quantization, whereas this paper analyzes the mechanistic interpretability of natural language user profiles on open-weight language models.

papers.t: The Missing Complement: State-Conditioned Minimal Sufficient Evidence for Coding Agents
papers.idea: Retrieval for coding agents often yields redundant context by ranking items independently. The paper frames retrieval as recovering the complement of evidence needed for an agent's next step given its current state. MSS-Complement constructs a jointly sufficient set of evidence items via three semantic calls rather than individual ranking.
papers.link: Both aim to refine the candidate selection process. UNIQUE eliminates cascade retrieval stages through discrete code generation, while this paper selects non-redundant contextual sets for coding agents using state-conditioned complements.

papers.t: Think Thrice Before Reranking: Multi-perspective Evidence and Reasoning Integration for Text Reranking
papers.idea: Single reasoning trajectories in LLM rerankers cause cascading errors and miss multifaceted relevance signals. The authors introduce a multi-trajectory reasoning space that evaluates queries and documents through complementary perspectives such as semantic alignment, intent satisfaction, and evidence grounding. A unified generative model synthesizes these trajectories and optimizes ranking via progressive reinforcement learning.
papers.link: Both explore ranking architectures. UNIQUE relies on joint discrete code prediction and discriminative scoring for speed, whereas this paper uses multi-path text reasoning and reinforcement learning for deep listwise reranking.

papers.t: Reasoning Quality Matters: Combating Reasoning Collapse in LLM-based Embedding Learning
papers.idea: CoFree counters reasoning collapse in LLM text embeddings using a two-stage training approach. It first restores reasoning capabilities via reference-guided supervised fine-tuning while retaining representation strength. Next, it applies reinforcement learning with dual rewards that balance embedding similarity with reasoning quality.
papers.link: Both train representation spaces for search and retrieval. UNIQUE learns discrete feedback-aware quantization codes, whereas CoFree fine-tunes continuous dense embeddings to retain multi-step reasoning capabilities.

papers.t: Verify, Don't Trust: Agentic Model Development for Video Discovery Retrieval at Scale
papers.idea: EvoPilot automates long-horizon machine learning experimentation across distributed retrieval systems. It enforces human gating and artifact verification rather than unconstrained prompt-driven loops to prevent misleading comparisons across varying software and data snapshots.
papers.link: Both address candidate retrieval in industrial web services. UNIQUE unifies retrieval and ranking stages within a single neural model, while EvoPilot automates distributed training workflows and offline validation for two-tower video search models.

papers.t: Hybrid GPU-CPU Retrieval for Personalized Search at Ultra-Large Scale
papers.idea: The paper presents a heterogeneous co-serving architecture for large-scale personalized search. A GPU pathway runs deep two-tower retrieval with interaction pre-ranking over a curated billion-scale document pool. Simultaneously, an efficient CPU pathway executes lightweight embedding matching over an index twenty times larger.
papers.link: Both aim to serve candidates efficiently at web scale. UNIQUE replaces multi-stage systems with a unified quantizer, whereas this paper maintains decoupled stages via heterogeneous GPU-CPU systems serving two-tower embeddings.

papers.t: Auto-Bidding with Disentangled Advertiser Profiles and Train-Free Adaptation
papers.idea: ADAPT personalizes auto-bidding policies using disentangled advertiser profiles and training-free adaptation. It extracts static and dynamic profiles using memory-bank contrastive learning, separates dynamic profiles into shared and private components, and conditions a Decision Transformer on them. New advertisers receive prototype profiles and existing profiles update through exponential moving average without retraining.
papers.link: Both optimize behavior modeling in commercial platforms. UNIQUE unifies retrieval and ranking architectures, whereas ADAPT uses disentangled user representations and Decision Transformers to learn bidding strategies for online advertising.

papers.t: Adaptive Preference Modeling via Explicit Indirect Relational Learning for Personalized Fashion Matching
papers.idea: APCL formulates personalized fashion matching by explicitly modeling both direct and indirect relationships across users and items. It constructs indirect personalization and compatibility views via correlation-guided aggregation over multimodal features. Contrastive learning aligns direct and indirect representations to maintain consistency across relational contexts.
papers.link: Both generate candidate items based on historical interaction sequences. UNIQUE operates through end-to-end discrete quantization, whereas APCL extracts direct and indirect multimodal graph relations using contrastive learning.

papers.t: Predictable Failure in Multi-Hop Retrieval: Score-Distributional Confidence Scoring and Abstention
papers.idea: Multi-hop retrieval often fails silently without signalling incomplete context. The authors introduce the Confident-Wrong-Answer Rate metric and train a logistic model over nine zero-cost query-time score distribution features. This model yields calibrated confidence scores that guide selective retrieval abstention.
papers.link: Both inspect ranking reliability in multi-step setups. UNIQUE avoids error cascades by replacing hierarchical identifiers with flat quantization, while this paper develops confidence scoring over score distributions to trigger search abstention.

papers.t: Scoring With the Engine: Retrieval Exposure, Cross-Engine Divergence, and the Limits of Engine-Agnostic GEO Scores
papers.idea: The paper investigates whether deterministic, engine-agnostic scores can proxy generative search visibility. Through an empirical audit of four live AI search surfaces across 15 commercial prompts, it shows near-zero cross-engine URL overlap. The study proposes measuring page fit, engine exposure, and final visibility as distinct components.
papers.link: Both evaluate retrieval and ranking outputs. UNIQUE engineers an end-to-end feed recommendation architecture, whereas this paper audits generative web search visibility to separate engine exposure from page relevance.

papers.t: Beyond Raw Engagement: A Counterfactual Observability Framework for Recommender Systems at Netflix
papers.idea: The paper presents a counterfactual observability framework deployed at Netflix for recommender systems. It models observability as a counterfactual estimation problem using logged exploration probabilities. This approach separates content quality from presentation bias and measures incrementality across single-stage and cascading pipelines.
papers.link: Both analyze multi-stage recommendation pipelines. UNIQUE collapses retrieval and ranking into a single model, whereas this paper builds counterfactual logging techniques to evaluate separate stages within existing cascading pipelines.

papers.t: Parameterized Dense-Sparse Fusion for Hybrid Retrieval: Tuning a Rank-Score Mix on BEIR SciFact with Qdrant
papers.idea: The paper defines a parameterized hybrid retrieval scoring family that combines dense cosine and sparse BM42 lists. It tunes weights for dense priors, rank-versus-score mix, and RRF smoothing via grid search on training splits before evaluation. Experiments across BEIR datasets show tuned fusion outperforms equal-weight RRF and dense-only retrieval.
papers.link: Both develop methods to improve candidate selection. UNIQUE replaces two-stage setups with a unified generative model, whereas this paper tunes fusion formulas across distinct dense vector indices and sparse lexical indices.

papers.t: Per-Query Gating of LLM Rerankers for Multi-Hop Retrieval
papers.idea: A learned classifier skips expensive LLM reranking calls in graph-augmented multi-hop retrieval. The gate predicts whether an initial retriever or a cheap distilled scorer already contains the target passage using pre-retrieval score distributions and query features. Across benchmarks, it reduces reranker calls by half with minor retrieval coverage losses.
papers.link: Both target computational efficiency in retrieval and ranking. UNIQUE trains a single model for both tasks, whereas this paper trains a classifier gate to skip heavy reranking stages when simpler retrievers are sufficient.

papers.t: Inherit4Rec: Parameter Inheritance for Efficient Scaling of Recommendation Models
papers.idea: Inherit4Rec expands recommendation models without training from scratch on streaming data. It supports dense-to-dense growth via hybrid parameter initialization with asymmetric training and dense-to-sparse conversion via co-activation-aware partitioning into sparse mixture-of-experts networks.
papers.link: Both scale neural architectures for streaming recommendations. UNIQUE focuses on structural quantization to merge retrieval and ranking, whereas Inherit4Rec focuses on parameter initialization to convert dense backbones into sparse mixture-of-experts.

papers.t: From Prompt to Recommendation: A Fitted Stage Model of Brand Visibility in AI Search
papers.idea: The paper models brand mentions in generative search engines through a multistage visibility pipeline. It decomposes mentions into prompt-page match, retrieval exposure, selection, and model prior knowledge. Analysis across thousands of repeated runs indicates that engine retrieval exposure and prior persistence dominate mention probabilities over raw query-agnostic page relevance.
papers.link: Both study the decomposition of candidate retrieval pipelines. UNIQUE replaces the multi-stage cascade with a unified network, while this paper models visibility across cascading retrieval stages in generative AI search.

papers.t: Semantic Candidate-Job Matching: A Comparative Evaluation of Dense Embedding Models in Hybrid Retrieval
papers.idea: The paper evaluates dense embedding models for candidate-job matching in staffing workflows. It fine-tunes EmbeddingGemma using Cached Multiple Negatives Ranking Loss and combines dense vector similarity with sparse BM25 retrieval using Reciprocal Rank Fusion.
papers.link: Both tackle candidate retrieval and matching. UNIQUE applies end-to-end vector quantization for feed recommendations, whereas this paper fine-tunes bi-encoder text embeddings to match resumes with job postings via hybrid retrieval.

papers.t: From Ranked Documents to Reliable Contexts: An Answer-Oriented Context Construct Framework for AI Search
papers.idea: AI search shifts the consumer of retrieved text from human users to generative models. This paper introduces an answer-oriented context construction framework that refines candidate documents using answer support, content trustworthiness, and set-level context organization. The framework transforms ranked lists into structured context to improve LLM generation.
papers.link: Both rethink how retrieved lists are fed to downstream models. UNIQUE uses generated item codes directly for discriminative scoring, whereas this work restructures ranked passages into non-redundant contexts for generative question answering.

papers.t: PSD: Pseudo Self-Distillation of Memory Representation Capabilities for LLM Agents
papers.idea: Pseudo Self-Distillation transfers memory construction capabilities from a black-box oracle LLM into small language models. A single small model serves as both teacher and student, where the teacher receives the oracle output in a privileged prompt. The student learns to match the teacher's distribution using only the task prompt, eliminating reliance on proprietary models during deployment.
papers.link: Both employ sequence representations to optimize efficiency. UNIQUE uses single-layer quantized codes for recommendations, while PSD distills agent memory structures from large models into small student networks.

papers.t: Beyond Relevance: Structured Semantic Supervision for Product Search with LLM-Augmented Annotations
papers.idea: The paper augments product search data with structured LLM-generated attributes, explanations, and human centrality annotations. It trains a dual-encoder retriever and MLP re-ranker using these semantic features to distinguish central products from loosely related items.
papers.link: Both optimize industrial search and candidate ranking. UNIQUE combines generative retrieval and ranking using discrete codes, whereas this paper enhances dual encoders and MLP rerankers with synthetic LLM attribute annotations.

papers.t: MuSeR: Scalable Long-sequence Recommendation with Multi-interest Modeling
papers.idea: MuSeR performs candidate retrieval over ultra-long user behavioral histories for industrial recommenders. It compresses sequence history via hierarchical temporal pooling, extracts diverse user interests through orthogonal multi-query attention, and aligns sparse item IDs with multimodal text summaries distilled from large language models.
papers.link: Both model long-sequence candidate retrieval for industrial recommenders. UNIQUE generates discrete quantization tokens to perform retrieval and ranking together, whereas MuSeR extracts multi-interest vector embeddings to search external approximate nearest-neighbor indexes.

papers.t: UNIQUE: A Unified Retrieval and Ranking System for Large-Scale Feed Recommendation
papers.idea: UNIQUE unifies retrieval and ranking into a single framework using end-to-end quantization. It replaces hierarchical semantic identifiers with feedback-aware single-layer flat quantization to prevent error propagation and represent long-tail items. The architecture combines generative code prediction for candidate retrieval with target-code-aware discriminative scoring for ranking.
papers.link: The centre of this map: of the 200 papers, it has the most in common with the rest.

papers.t: A Redundancy Reduction Approach for Controllable Sequential Recommendations
papers.idea: The paper regularizes sequential recommendation models using feature decorrelation objectives to reduce representation redundancy without negative sampling. This non-contrastive approach reshapes user and item embedding geometries to balance head and tail item exposure. It controls the trade-off between recommendation precision and catalog diversity.
papers.link: Both address representation issues in sequential recommenders. UNIQUE uses single-layer quantization to capture long-tail items, whereas this paper applies non-contrastive feature decorrelation to reshape user-item embedding spaces.

papers.t: Graded-Relevance Composed Multimodal Retrieval for E-commerce Visual Search at Scale
papers.idea: GradCIR trains early-fusion vision-language retrievers using graded ordinal relevance for composed visual search. It aligns composed multimodal queries of images and text modifiers against catalog items across multiple match levels rather than binary labels. The framework uses fine-grained training objectives to preserve near-match rankings at scale.
papers.link: Both build candidate retrieval architectures for e-commerce. UNIQUE uses unified generative quantization for user feeds, while GradCIR uses early-fusion vision-language transformers with graded relevance for composed image retrieval.

papers.t: Auditing Source Exposure in Baidu and Google AI Search
papers.idea: This paper audits AI-generated search overviews across Baidu and Google using paired English and Chinese queries. It tracks triggering frequency, visible source domains, source concentration, and domain overlap between platforms. It also evaluates the semantic similarity of generated answers using text embeddings.
papers.link: Both study information retrieval architectures. UNIQUE proposes a quantised feed recommendation system, whereas this paper audits source visibility and concentration differences between commercial generative search platforms.

papers.t: What Makes a Good Semantic ID for Generative Recommendation? A Reproducibility Study
papers.idea: This paper presents a reproducibility study evaluating semantic ID designs for generative recommendation under a unified framework. It benchmarks representative semantic ID methods across standardized data splits and evaluation metrics. The experiments analyze codebook utilization, backbone scaling behavior, and semantic preservation.
papers.link: Both investigate discrete semantic identifiers in generative recommenders. While this study benchmarks traditional hierarchical RQ-VAE identifiers, UNIQUE abandons hierarchical trees entirely in favor of single-layer flat quantization to prevent error propagation.

papers.t: UK-PRBENCH: A Paragraph-Level Precedent Retrieval Benchmark for United Kingdom Case Law
papers.idea: The paper introduces a paragraph-level precedent retrieval benchmark for UK case law using judgments from the UK National Archives. It extracts citation instances across various courts and establishes retrieval baselines across multiple embedding and language models.
papers.link: Both examine candidate retrieval performance. UNIQUE introduces an industrial system for feed recommendations, whereas this paper provides a specialized benchmark and baseline embeddings for paragraph-level precedent retrieval in UK case law.

papers.t: GroundedGEO: Auditing the Evidence Gap in Generative Search Rankings
papers.idea: Generative search engines reward candidate pages with fabricated, query-aligned claims over unsupported honest text. The framework audits this identifiability gap by verifying candidate claims against an external evidence channel. It then reranks candidates using claim-level grounding scores to penalize unsupported relevance inflation.
papers.link: Both study candidate ranking dynamics. UNIQUE trains a unified recommendation model via quantization, whereas this paper audits generative search engines by scoring candidate claims against external factual evidence.

papers.t: Robust Fusion of Semantic and Behavioural Signals for LLM Reranking in Personalised Search
papers.idea: The paper integrates structured behavioural and statistical signals into LLM-based cross-encoder rerankers for personalised search. It serialises numerical interaction metrics and query slice statistics directly into prompt tokens. This allows the model to balance historical behavioural evidence on head queries with semantic generalization on long-tail queries.
papers.link: Both improve ranking for personalized recommendation and search. UNIQUE incorporates interaction signals via feedback-aware quantization, while this paper injects user interaction statistics directly as text tokens into an LLM cross-encoder.

papers.t: Knowledge-as-Skill: A Structural Design for Autonomous Knowledge-Base Use by LLM Agents
papers.idea: The paper organizes knowledge bases into discoverable, navigable skills for autonomous LLM agents instead of relying on fixed chunk retrieval. It structures data into three layers: a discovery layer with SKILL.md, a navigation layer with index files, and a knowledge layer of documents with descriptive YAML frontmatter. Agents inspect metadata, navigate hierarchies, and decide when to read full texts.
papers.link: Both systems retrieve relevant entities from structured indexes, but 2609.25991 focuses on agent-driven navigation of file metadata for QA. In contrast, 2609.23718 targets feed recommendation via end-to-end vector quantization that merges retrieval and scoring.

papers.t: Discovery-Driven Integration of Disjoint Tables via Text
papers.idea: LOKI integrates disjoint tables in data lakes using unstructured text documents without predefined schemas or links. It identifies fine-grained row-to-sentence associations using an encoder, then uses these links to discover join paths and materialize cross-table relations.
papers.link: Both methods process unstructured information to associate related entities, but 2609.26658 performs row-to-sentence linking to discover relational joins across data lakes. 2609.23718 designs quantized token indexes to retrieve and rank items directly for feed users.

papers.t: ItColBERT: An Italian-Specialised Late-Interaction Retriever
papers.idea: ItColBERT is an Italian-specialised late-interaction retriever trained with PyLate on a single consumer GPU. The training protocol uses supervised contrastive learning followed by single-teacher distillation from an initialized retrieval checkpoint. An empirical evaluation across four Italian benchmarks shows that inference-time chunking outperforms extended-length retraining for long-document retrieval.
papers.link: Both works optimize candidate retrieval architectures, but 2609.26856 specializes in token-level late-interaction encoders for document retrieval. 2609.23718 instead replaces dual-encoder retrieval with unified generative code generation and flat quantization.

papers.t: Distilling Lexical Product Associations into Deep Transformers: An Extreme Multi-Label Approach for Natural Language E-Commerce Search
papers.idea: The paper treats e-commerce product search as an extreme multi-label classification problem. It builds a pseudo-ground-truth item similarity graph using a TF-IDF teacher model and distills it into a DistilBERT student encoder using binary cross-entropy. This allows the transformer student to address vocabulary mismatch in natural language queries while predicting relevant catalog items.
papers.link: Both approaches tackle catalog retrieval by matching queries to items using transformer encoders, but 2609.26921 treats e-commerce search as extreme multi-label classification using TF-IDF distillation. 2609.23718 eliminates separate retrieval stages by using flat quantization to unify retrieval and ranking.

papers.t: Calibrating Reproduced Claims in Recommender Systems
papers.idea: This paper introduces claim calibration to determine the strongest scientific claim supported by a reproduction study. The authors analyze five original-reproduction study pairs in recommender systems and document discrepancies between numerical values, method rankings, and claims. They formulate the Claim Evidence Profile, a reporting structure that specifies the calibrated claim, testing conditions, and unresolved elements.
papers.link: Both papers examine recommender system models, but 2609.26975 investigates the reproducibility of published claims and evaluation protocols. 2609.23718 develops a model architecture for unified retrieval and ranking.

papers.t: Tie Handling Is Part of the Evaluation Protocol: An Order-Invariance Audit for Tie-Heavy Recommender Scores
papers.idea: Offline top-k evaluation metrics can artificially inflate when tied scores preserve input order and place relevant items first. The authors formalize row-order invariance, audit metric sensitivity across tie-breaking strategies, and derive exact expectations for Hit Rate and NDCG under uniform random tie-breaking.
papers.link: Both papers address ranking behavior in recommender systems, but 2609.26977 analyzes evaluation variance caused by tie-breaking strategies in top-k metrics. 2609.23718 focuses on model architecture and quantization for recommendation feeds.

papers.t: When LLM-Based User Profiling Adds Value in Production Streaming Recommendation
papers.idea: The paper evaluates content-based user profiling strategies for production streaming recommendation. It compares aggregate item embeddings against LLM-generated natural language summaries, testing both full-history and attention-fused temporal representations across diverse user behaviors.
papers.link: Both works model user behavior histories to generate personalized recommendations, but 2609.27183 studies LLM-generated summaries and pooling strategies for streaming feeds. 2609.23718 focuses on quantization-based indexing to unify generative candidate retrieval with ranking.

papers.t: BoundaryMORPH: Budgeted Reranking via Active Set Selection for Diffuse Retrieval
papers.idea: Retrieval-augmented generation for open-ended queries often requires filling context windows when cross-encoder evaluation budgets are smaller than context capacity. The method uses a Gaussian process surrogate over dual-encoder candidates to actively sample cross-encoder evaluations near the top-k boundary. Information updates across unscored candidates to select the final set of retrieved documents.
papers.link: Both systems address multi-stage candidate selection pipelines, but 2609.27213 uses active sampling and Gaussian processes to select candidates under a fixed reranker budget. 2609.23718 eliminates the two-stage boundary altogether by unifying retrieval and ranking in one quantized framework.

papers.t: Test-Time Adaptation with Query-Dependent Residuals for Visual Document Retrieval
papers.idea: Q-REACT adapts visual document retrieval at test time using sparse reranker feedback without modifying encoders or document indexes. It learns a shared low-rank transformation to produce query-dependent residual vectors and incorporates document-level context. The transformation is trained by distilling local reranker preferences normalized over the complete cached page index.
papers.link: Both papers adapt candidate representations using feedback, but 2609.27688 learns query-dependent residual vectors to update frozen multimodal document embeddings. 2609.23718 trains a single-layer flat quantizer with user feedback to jointly optimize candidate retrieval and ranking.

papers.t: Dual-Hypergraph Indexing: Bridging Knowledge Islands for Multi-Hop Reasoning in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.idea: Dual-Hypergraph Indexing connects fragmented hyperedges in retrieval-augmented generation. It builds a two-tiered hierarchy pairing a foundational factual hypergraph with an aggregated deep-insight hypergraph. The aggregation combines topological hub analysis for semantic clusters with sliding-window exploration for chronological progressions.
papers.link: Both approaches improve recall across dispersed items, but 2609.28108 builds two-tier hypergraphs to connect fragmented knowledge chunks for QA. 2609.23718 uses single-layer flat vector quantization to capture long-tail items in recommendation feeds.

papers.t: Beyond a Scalar: Distributional Serving Interfaces for Watch-Time Prediction
papers.idea: Watch-time prediction systems typically serve a single scalar mean, discarding critical information about video completion and exit behaviors. The distributional serving interface models joint distributions over derived event types and event times using duration support constraints. A frozen compact representation then serves downstream ranking and exposure decisions without retraining.
