papers.link: Both systems design ranking methods for industrial video and feed recommendation, but 2609.28383 addresses watch-time bias by estimating event distributions instead of scalar scores. 2609.23718 addresses retrieval-ranking alignment by unifying both tasks within a single quantized pipeline.

papers.t: OneTrans-V2: Unifying Retrieval, Pre-rank, and Fine-rank with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender
papers.idea: OneTrans-V2 unifies retrieval, pre-ranking, and fine-ranking stages into a single Transformer architecture. It encodes the user behavior sequence once as shared context while maintaining stage-specific candidate scoring. The architecture incorporates decision-conditioned generative retrieval, mixture-of-experts scaling, and sequence-native training to amortize context computation.
papers.link: Both systems collapse multi-stage recommendation cascades into a single Transformer architecture that generates candidate identifiers. While 2609.28589 relies on user-sequence context sharing across cascaded heads, 2609.23718 integrates feedback-aware flat quantization to replace hierarchical codes and avoid error propagation.

papers.t: The Fellowship of the Query: Learning Retrieval Actions
papers.idea: Small language models often struggle to control multi-step search trajectories in retrieval-augmented generation. This paper trains sub-3B parameter models using LoRA on accepted teacher trajectories to imitate a seven-action search-control protocol. The approach evaluates action prediction and end-to-end performance in multi-hop question answering.
papers.link: Both methods study sequential decision-making architectures, but 2609.28653 trains small models to orchestrate multi-step tool calls for question answering. 2609.23718 trains generative models to emit discrete item codes for feed retrieval.

papers.t: Cross-Country Code-Mixing for Generative Recommendation
papers.idea: Generative recommendation models struggle across country-specific markets because user interaction sequences and item identifiers are strictly partitioned. The method quantizes items into a shared semantic token space using both content and behavior signals, then performs token-level code-mixing on user behavior sequences. Dual constraints and context-aware adaptive reweighting ensure substitutions preserve both static and dynamic item properties.
papers.link: Both approaches apply vector quantization to map items into discrete token representations for generative recommendation. While 2609.28972 applies token-level code-mixing to align cross-country user sequences, 2609.23718 adopts single-layer flat quantization to unify retrieval and discriminative ranking without hierarchical errors.

papers.t: Seek: Self-Evaluative Exploration for Knowledge Retrieval
papers.idea: Seek performs multi-round retrieval by interleaving candidate retrieval with LLM-based assessment. In each round, an LLM evaluates retrieved passages, identifies missing information, and generates feedback-conditioned pseudo-passages to fetch fresh candidates. The process terminates and outputs a consolidated ranking once the query information need is satisfied.
papers.link: Both papers seek to enhance candidate selection, but 2609.28980 relies on iterative LLM critique and query reformulation to fetch documents. 2609.23718 relies on end-to-end quantized code generation and discriminative scoring within a single recommendation model.

papers.t: X-Rec Technical Report
papers.idea: X-Rec formulates next-item recommendation by directly modeling continuous item embedding distributions with flow matching. It generates embedding triggers for approximate nearest neighbor retrieval rather than relying on discrete tokens or single-vector user embeddings. The architecture applies Riemannian flow matching on hyperspherical embeddings and limits iterative velocity updates to the final Transformer layer.
papers.link: Both frameworks address next-item recommendation by modernizing candidate generation beyond classical semantic identifiers. 2609.29180 bypasses discrete tokens entirely to model continuous embeddings via flow matching, whereas 2609.23718 refines discrete representation using feedback-aware single-layer quantization.

papers.t: ScalarLens: Numerical Embeddings with Stable Coordinates and Contextual Responses for CTR Prediction
papers.idea: ScalarLens decouples numerical feature representation into stable coordinates and sample-specific contextual responses for click-through rate prediction. It learns representations directly from numerical values on their original scale without external normalizers. This preserves scalar coordinate ordering while adapting predictive meanings across contexts.
papers.link: Both works target click-through rate optimization in large-scale systems, but 2609.29182 designs non-linear embeddings to preserve the geometry of numerical features. 2609.23718 unifies the candidate generation step with the ranking stage using discrete item quantization.

papers.t: Asymmetric Dynamic Routing: Balancing Reasoning Depth and Computational Efficiency in Hypergraph RAG
papers.idea: Asymmetric Dynamic Routing adapts graph retrieval to question complexity across a hierarchical dual-hypergraph. A lightweight intent classifier directs queries into localized anchoring, bottom-up adjacency diffusion, or top-down insight grounding. This query-conditioned routing prevents over-retrieval on simple questions while preserving context for abstract reasoning tasks.
papers.link: Both methods route queries based on retrieval needs, but 2609.29282 navigates hierarchical hypergraphs dynamically to handle complex multi-hop questions. 2609.23718 unifies candidate retrieval and ranking for recommendation through generative code prediction.

papers.t: A Systematic Multi-Domain Evaluation of Document Retrievers
papers.idea: The paper presents a systematic empirical evaluation of sparse, dense, and expansion-based document retrieval models across multiple domain benchmarks. It measures retrieval effectiveness alongside query runtimes and failure points under uniform compute budgets using public model artifacts.
papers.link: Both studies evaluate retrieval efficiency and effectiveness, but 2609.29455 benchmarks standard dense and sparse passage retrievers across varied text domains. 2609.23718 builds a specialized unified model for industrial feed recommendation.

papers.t: OBLIQ-IR: Training a Dense Retriever for Oblique Queries
papers.idea: Dense retrievers struggle when document relevance depends on latent attributes rather than topical overlap. This paper trains a bi-encoder using synthetic queries tailored to oblique retrieval mechanisms alongside kNN-graph distillation from a frozen authorship model. The resulting retriever improves first-stage candidate retrieval on non-topical benchmarks.
papers.link: Both papers seek to improve first-stage candidate retrieval, but 2609.29649 trains bi-encoders on synthetic queries to retrieve documents based on non-topical stylistic traits. 2609.23718 constructs a unified generative retrieval and ranking architecture based on quantized item codes.

papers.t: SEEK: Skill-Routed Evaluation with Evolvable Knowledge for Industrial Search
papers.idea: SEEK automates search quality evaluation by routing queries to an evolvable bank of externalized skills instead of hardcoding evaluation rules into prompts or model weights. A skill-aligned model assesses page-level search result quality and identifies causes of degradation. A self-evolving skill bank adapts over time to reflect changing policies and intents.
papers.link: Both papers consider industrial search or recommendation setups, but 2609.29803 builds an evolving evaluation agent to audit search engine result pages. 2609.23718 develops a unified retrieval and ranking model for feed recommendation.

papers.t: LSF-SR: Latent Semantic Fusion for Sequential Recommendation via Flow-based Conditional Variational Autoencoders
papers.idea: Sequential recommendation models face representation misalignment when combining collaborative interaction IDs with LLM-derived semantic features. LSF-SR uses a conditional variational autoencoder equipped with stacked normalizing flows to generate flexible posterior distributions for semantic fusion. A dynamic KL annealing schedule mitigates posterior collapse during training.
papers.link: Both papers model user interaction histories for sequential recommendation, but 2609.29815 uses conditional variational autoencoders and normalizing flows to align LLM semantics with ID embeddings. 2609.23718 combines retrieval and ranking into one pipeline using single-layer flat quantization.

papers.t: Learning Better Reasoning for Generative Recommendation with Semantic IDs
papers.idea: Generative recommendation models often suffer from misleading reasoning trajectories that harm next-item prediction. The paper introduces a pipeline that aligns language models with semantic item IDs, applies best-of-N rejection sampling for supervised fine-tuning, and optimizes reasoning using constrained ranking.
papers.link: Both works investigate generative recommender systems that represent items with discrete semantic tokens. 2609.29973 optimizes reasoning trajectories over fixed semantic IDs using rejection sampling, while 2609.23718 abandons hierarchical semantic IDs in favor of flat quantization that is co-optimized with ranking.

papers.t: Nearest but Not Dearest: Shared Curator-Feedback Infrastructure for Content-Only Search and Recommendation
papers.idea: Content-only music discovery stacks using vector similarity often retrieve tracks that sound close but fail contextual criteria like language or holiday themes. The authors address this by collecting structured curator failure labels on candidate pairs. They use this feedback to route errors between acoustic embedding updates and contextual metadata filtering.
papers.link: Both works use interaction signals to correct retrieval errors, but 2609.30568 relies on curator failure labels to separate vector errors from metadata filters in music search. 2609.23718 trains a flat quantizer end-to-end on user feedback to prevent error cascading across stages.

papers.t: Embedding Subspace Partitioning for Dynamic Multi-Objective Retrieval
papers.idea: Multi-objective first-stage retrieval suffers from representational conflict in monolithic embedding spaces. Embedding Subspace Partitioning divides the embedding into task-specific subspaces, each assigned to an objective. A weighted combination of per-subspace dot products enables trade-off tuning at inference time without model retraining.
papers.link: Both methods address candidate retrieval trade-offs in first-stage matching, but 2609.30601 partitions embedding spaces into target subspaces for multi-objective vector search. 2609.23718 unifies retrieval with ranking using generative code predictions and target-code discriminative scoring.

papers.t: Component Benchmark: Hierarchical Model Profiling for Large-scale Recommendation Systems
papers.idea: Component Benchmark isolates and benchmarks submodules of large recommendation systems in a hierarchical tree. It runs on a single GPU using real data distributions to capture dynamic input shapes and operator inefficiencies. Practitioners can map latency, memory use, and hardware utilization directly to architectural model components.
papers.link: Both works examine large-scale industrial recommender architectures, but 2609.30656 provides a benchmarking tool to profile hardware performance across submodules. 2609.23718 proposes an architectural framework to consolidate the multi-stage cascade into a single model.

papers.t: Recommendation World Models for Future-State Control
papers.idea: UA-TWM attaches a consequence-modeling interface to a frozen sequential recommender to steer future user states. It generates candidate slate actions around a reference slate, predicts their utility, target gains, and failure risks, and selects an action subject to utility constraints. The reference slate serves as a fallback when candidate slates fail qualification tests.
papers.link: Both frameworks address sequential recommendation pipelines, but 2609.30711 learns a world model over frozen recommenders to control user state transitions across slates. 2609.23718 designs an end-to-end model that integrates retrieval and ranking via quantization.

papers.t: RecToolBench: Benchmarking Recommendation-Specific Tool Orchestration under Fuzzy User Intent
papers.idea: RecToolBench benchmarks tool-using recommender agents that operate under fuzzy user instructions. The benchmark generates tasks across four orchestration complexity levels using the Model Context Protocol. Trajectories are evaluated through rule-based execution verification and rubric-based model judging.
papers.link: Both studies focus on recommender systems, but 2609.30717 benchmarks LLM agents executing tool calls under fuzzy user queries. 2609.23718 develops an end-to-end serving architecture that fuses retrieval and ranking for industrial feeds.

papers.t: QReason: Query-Focused Decoupled Chain-of-Thought for Efficient Passage Reranking
papers.idea: Listwise passage rerankers repeat chain-of-thought generation across sliding windows, causing redundant computation. QReason decouples query reasoning from passage comparison by training a dedicated rewriter that produces a reasoning-expanded query once. A non-reasoning reranker then reuses this reasoning query across all passage windows.
papers.link: Both papers aim to reduce latency across the candidate scoring pipeline, but 2609.30904 decouples query reasoning from passage reranking to speed up text search. 2609.23718 collapses retrieval and ranking stages into a single model using quantized token predictions.

papers.t: KuaFu: Compressing Long User Behavior into Understanding at Billion Scale
papers.idea: KuaFu compresses long user behavior logs into compact semantic memory tokens using an item-level encoder and adapter. A frozen large language model decoder consumes the interleaved memory, action, and task tokens to generate user profiles and attributes. It trains the pipeline through multi-stage objectives and hallucination-aware reinforcement learning.
papers.link: Both methods condense extensive user behavior to serve large-scale recommendations, but 2609.31045 aggregates user interactions into semantic memory tokens for LLM profile generation. 2609.23718 focuses on quantizing item identifiers into discrete codes to unify candidate retrieval with ranking.

papers.t: SPADE: Escaping the Popularity-Similarity Frontier to Measure Serendipitous Recommendations
papers.idea: SPADE evaluates serendipity in recommender systems by combining user historical similarity, global popularity, and relevance. It maps items to a two-dimensional popularity-similarity space and constructs a user-specific Pareto frontier. The metric scores recommendations using the minimum Euclidean distance from this frontier for correctly predicted test items.
papers.link: Both papers address feed recommendation challenges, but 2609.31164 introduces a geometric metric to measure serendipity and popularity bias. 2609.23718 focuses on unified retrieval and ranking model design using flat vector quantization.

papers.t: AgentRecommender: LLM Agents Enable Customizable Recommender Systems on the User Side
papers.idea: AgentRecommender builds customizable, user-side recommender systems that run independently of platform algorithms. It uses the world knowledge and investigation abilities of LLM agents to infer item attributes zero-shot without external labels or full platform data.
papers.link: Both works aim to improve personalized item selection, but 2609.31166 builds user-side LLM agents to infer preferences independent of platform models. 2609.23718 focuses on platform-side infrastructure, unifying feed retrieval and ranking into a single framework.

papers.t: Enriching Sequential Recommendation with Graph Laplacian Positional Embeddings
papers.idea: The authors integrate global item relationships into sequential recommendation models without adding extra training parameters. They build an item co-occurrence graph, calculate eigenvectors of its normalized graph Laplacian, and use these fixed spectral coordinates in place of standard learnable sequence positional embeddings in SASRec.
papers.link: Both papers improve candidate matching for sequential recommendation, but 2609.31253 incorporates graph Laplacian eigenvectors as positional embeddings in SASRec. 2609.23718 replaces multi-stage sequential pipelines with a unified generative and discriminative model driven by flat quantization.

papers.t: Retail Product Search: A Practical Approach at Target
papers.idea: A production retail search system combines parallel lexical matching and dense vector retrieval using a fine-tuned dual encoder. The system applies a precision control mechanism to suppress irrelevant semantic results and merges candidate lists via rank fusion. The architecture serves production traffic at scale across web and mobile platforms.
papers.link: Both papers describe large-scale production retrieval architectures, but 2609.31498 combines lexical search and dual encoders using rank fusion for e-commerce. 2609.23718 replaces multi-stage pipelines with unified generative code retrieval and ranking.

papers.t: Data Processing for Offline Evaluation in Recommender Systems: a Survey
papers.idea: This paper presents a systematic survey and unified taxonomy of data processing practices for offline evaluation in recommender systems. It formalises the pipeline from dataset selection and multimodal feature extraction to data filtering and splitting strategies. The work analyzes experimental trends and identifies inconsistencies across common evaluation protocols.
papers.link: Both papers focus on the recommendation domain, but 2609.31696 provides a survey of data processing and evaluation protocols for offline benchmarks. 2609.23718 proposes an architectural solution that unifies the retrieval and ranking stages.

papers.t: MM-VeriRec: Failure-Guided Fusion for Verifiable Agentic Multimodal Recommendation
papers.idea: MM-VeriRec evaluates agentic multimodal recommendation under hidden visual constraints. It introduces a deterministic verifier that detects visual contradictions, invalid items, and impossible requests. The system then uses explicit failure labels to guide multimodal fusion and abstention strategies.
papers.link: Both papers evaluate complex recommendation scenarios, but 2609.31718 develops verification tools to handle visual contradictions in multimodal requests. 2609.23718 develops a quantized model structure to unify retrieval and ranking in high-volume feed environments.

papers.t: Overview of the TREC 2025 Million Large Language Models track
papers.idea: This benchmark shifts the classic retrieval target from static documents to specialized language models. Systems use a discovery set of queries, responses, and log-probabilities from over one thousand models to learn behavioral expertise representations. For new test queries, systems must rank candidate models by expected competence.
papers.link: Both works tackle large-scale candidate ranking, but 2609.31921 designs a benchmark to select and rank specialized LLMs based on competency. 2609.23718 creates a single neural system that jointly retrieves and scores user feed items.

papers.t: Recipe-Matching, Not Equivalence
papers.idea: This paper investigates synthetic LLM benchmark evaluation for mathematical retrieval. It trains embedding models on pairs generated using the benchmark's exact creation procedure versus algebra-verified pairs. The experiments show that models learn LLM artifact fingerprints and pair structures rather than genuine mathematical equivalence.
papers.link: Both works critique common indexing and evaluation assumptions, but 2609.31927 analyzes how mathematical retrieval benchmarks encourage synthetic pattern matching over true reasoning. 2609.23718 remedies semantic identifier failure modes in recommendation by swapping hierarchical trees for flat quantization.

papers.t: When Does Dense Retrieval Need Asymmetric Geometry? A Bias-Variance Theory of Shared and Dual Projections
papers.idea: This paper establishes a bias-variance theory for choosing between shared symmetric projections and unconstrained dual projections in dense retrieval. Shared projections restrict scoring to positive-semidefinite matrices, whereas dual projections introduce estimation variance. The authors formulate a decision boundary and propose CARS, an estimator that selects the optimal projection geometry from training data.
papers.link: Both papers examine the mathematical design of retrieval representations, but 2609.32488 analyzes the bias-variance trade-off between shared and dual projection matrices for dense bi-encoders. 2609.23718 departs from bi-encoder retrieval entirely, combining generative code prediction with discriminative ranking.

papers.t: Concepts Complement Dense Semantics: Learning Compact Sparse Spaces for Text-Image Retrieval
papers.idea: Dense vision-language models often miss fine-grained entities and visual attributes. This work learns a compact sparse concept space instead of using a full vocabulary. The sparse branch projects images and text into grounding-relevant concepts, complementing dense retrieval.
papers.link: Both papers use learned discrete or quantized units to complement continuous matching, but 2609.32671 projects multimodal features into sparse concept spaces for image-text retrieval. 2609.23718 employs flat vector quantization to index feed items for unified retrieval and ranking.

papers.t: RandSlot: Learning Compact Visual Document Representations with Random Soft Tokens
papers.idea: RandSlot compacts visual document representations by appending random unit soft tokens to query and document inputs during training. The encoder contextualizes these resampled auxiliary inputs alongside the content into a small set of retrieval vectors optimized via late interaction. At inference time, replacing the random tokens with fixed zero vectors retains performance without requiring runtime sampling.
papers.link: Both architectures rely on compact representations to scale retrieval, but 2609.32699 learns compact multi-vector visual representations via random soft tokens for late interaction. 2609.23718 uses single-layer vector quantization to discretize item representations for feed recommendation.

papers.t: Mend the Measurement Gap: Latent User Preference Modeling for Short-Form Video Recommendation
papers.idea: This paper addresses the measurement gap between observed implicit engagement signals and underlying user preferences in short-form video feeds. It introduces the Factorized Latent Value Model, which adds a structured measurement layer between raw behaviors and ranking. The method uses a supervised Gaussian variational bottleneck to infer latent preference states from noisy, duration-biased interactions.
papers.link: Both papers optimize industrial short-form video recommendation feeds, but 2609.32839 focuses on modeling latent satisfaction behind biased engagement signals using variational bottlenecks. 2609.23718 focuses on eliminating pipeline cascade mismatches by consolidating retrieval and ranking into one quantized network.

papers.t: PILAR: A Page-Grounded Unified Evidence Representation via an Entity-Linked Assertion Graph for Open-Domain QA Agents over Multimodal Document Corpora
papers.idea: The paper maps text, table, and figure facts into a shared, entity-linked assertion graph grounded in document pages. Question-answering agents use the graph to retrieve and expand page-level evidence across multimodal document corpora. Controlled graph traversal connects cross-document information while maintaining local page contexts for reading models.
papers.link: Both methods organize complex entity relations for retrieval, but 2609.32895 constructs multi-modal assertion graphs across documents for QA agents. 2609.23718 structures an item catalog using single-layer vector quantization to serve feed recommendations.

papers.t: Overview and Analysis of the RecSys Challenge 2026: Conversational Music Recommendation
papers.idea: This paper presents the overview and evaluation for the RecSys Challenge 2026 on conversational music recommendation. Systems retrieve and rank tracks across multi-turn dialogues while generating natural language responses. The authors evaluate participant architectures across dialogue depth, user cold-start settings, and goal specificity.
papers.link: Both papers involve candidate retrieval and item scoring, but 2609.33045 analyzes conversational music recommendation over multi-turn dialogues. 2609.23718 focuses on unified architectural modeling for non-conversational recommendation feeds.

papers.t: Inspire: Benchmarking Scientific Literature Search for Open Research Problems
papers.idea: Inspire benchmarks LLM agents searching scientific literature for open research problems. Each instance presents a solution-redacted research brief with a historical cutoff date. Agents search an open corpus to retrieve and rank graded antecedents, allowing diagnostic evaluation across resource exposure, selection, and ranking stages.
papers.link: Both works concern candidate search, but 2609.33233 evaluates autonomous agents searching academic literature for research problems. 2609.23718 targets consumer feed recommendation through generative code indexing.

papers.t: What Gets Measured Gets Managed: Sign-aware Recommendation Needs Sign-aware Evaluation
papers.idea: Current sign-aware recommender systems fail to distinguish liked from disliked items at inference because inner-product scoring cannot extract valence information. Standard ranking metrics assign zero utility to disliked items, masking negative recommendation infiltration. The paper introduces signed evaluation metrics that penalize disliked items and uses an auxiliary sign loss to restore valence awareness.
papers.link: Both papers study item scoring metrics and user preferences, but 2609.33346 addresses how inner-product models fail to distinguish disliked items by designing sign-aware ranking losses. 2609.23718 resolves retrieval-ranking disconnects by sharing quantized item representations across both phases.

papers.t: From PDF to Evidence: Structure-Aware Retrieval for Clinical Practice Guidelines
papers.idea: The method extracts evidence from clinical guideline PDFs by parsing page images into layout elements rather than flat text chunks. It builds structure-aware retrieval units for sections, table rows, flowchart paths, and graded recommendations while preserving hierarchical context. Element-level retrieval directs search to precise evidence structures instead of full pages.
papers.link: Both methods reformulate index representations to avoid error cascades, but 2609.33447 parses PDF visual layouts into structural components for clinical QA. 2609.23718 uses feedback-aware flat quantization on item embeddings to eliminate hierarchical retrieval errors in feed recommenders.

papers.t: Beyond the Beam: Constructive Repair and Candidate Completion for Generative Recommendation
papers.idea: Generative recommenders can miss valid new items during beam search retrieval after catalog expansion. The authors characterize assignment repair limits, formulating minimum-replacement identifier repair as a network flow problem. At inference, candidate completion uses prefix score bounds and collaborative corrections to search beyond the beam and certify top-k items.
papers.link: Both papers investigate generative recommendation models based on semantic item identifiers. While 2609.33745 remedies beam search failures by using network flow repairs and candidate completion over hierarchical identifiers, 2609.23718 avoids hierarchical error propagation by switching to single-layer flat quantization.

papers.t: STITCH-RAG: Spatio-Temporal Influence Tracing over Topic Hypergraphs for Multi-Hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.idea: The method constructs a semi-merged topic hypergraph that models multi-entity participation as topic hyperedges while retaining per-chunk entity descriptions. It propagates relevance across topic hyperedges and name-equivalent entity mentions via spatio-temporal influence bridging. The resulting continuous scores seed a localized Personalized PageRank algorithm to retrieve connected evidence chunks for multi-hop question answering.
papers.link: Both methods process multi-hop associations to link candidate entities, but 2609.34127 propagates influence across topic hypergraphs for question answering. 2609.23718 uses a quantized sequence model to retrieve and rank items in personal recommendation feeds.

papers.t: RidgeRank: Efficient Visual Document Reranking via Score Fusion and a Shallow Linear Readout
papers.idea: Multimodal language models serve as visual document rerankers but introduce high latency. RidgeRank accelerates reranking through early exit with a linear readout vector fitted via centered ridge regression to emulate full-depth scores. It then restores missing relevance information using a closed-form fusion rule that combines retriever and reranker scores.
papers.link: Both methods streamline multi-stage scoring pipelines, but 2609.34192 accelerates multimodal reranking by extracting early linear readouts from vision-language models. 2609.23718 unifies the candidate retrieval and ranking stages entirely using end-to-end quantization.

papers.t: Measuring and Mitigating Identity-Cue Preference Drift in LLM-based Recommender Systems
papers.idea: Large language model recommenders shift recommendations toward group stereotypes when demographic cues are added to prompts, despite unchanged interaction histories. PromptShift quantifies this identity-cue preference drift in list membership and directional group popularity. It mitigates the drift without retraining via adaptive post-hoc reranking based on user history mainstreamness.
papers.link: Both papers address personalized recommendation and reranking. UNIQUE unifies retrieval and ranking using quantized codes and generative scoring, whereas this paper uses an external post-hoc reranker to mitigate demographic preference drift in large language model prompts.

papers.t: SPRINT: Single-Step Generative Recommendation via Average Probability Velocity
papers.idea: Generative recommendation models using semantic IDs usually take multiple forward passes to predict token sequences. SPRINT frames semantic ID generation through average probability velocity, showing this velocity is determined by the average generation probability of each token. A bidirectional Transformer predicts all token probabilities in a single forward pass, optimized with a dual-level flow contrastive loss to enforce inter-token coherence.
papers.link: Both methods explore generative recommendation based on discrete item identifiers. While UNIQUE adopts a single-layer flat quantization scheme to avoid multi-step error accumulation, SPRINT retains multi-token semantic IDs and generates them simultaneously in a single forward pass via probability velocity.

papers.t: Correcting to Predict: Pseudo-Value Correction for Multimodal Attribute Value Extraction
papers.idea: C2P extracts multimodal product attribute values by training models to correct noisy pseudo-values. The system fine-tunes a multimodal model on correction targets generated via self-consistency. At inference time, it operates as a single-pass extraction step using a fixed placeholder.
papers.link: Both works handle e-commerce and catalog item representations. UNIQUE focuses on end-to-end user recommendation via discrete quantization, while this paper focuses on multimodal attribute extraction from product metadata using self-consistency correction.

papers.t: Relevance-Resolution Transfer via Scale-Decomposable Fractional Diffusion for Multi-Length Cross-Modal Hash Retrieval
papers.idea: MultiBit transfers multi-label semantic relevance into multi-length binary hash codes. It builds a fractional diffusion relation teacher over continuous scales using label co-occurrence and specificity. These continuous scales map to nested bit subblocks to preserve candidate rankings across different Hamming code lengths.
papers.link: Both approaches use discrete representation learning to index and retrieve items. UNIQUE applies single-layer flat vector quantization to recommendation retrieval and ranking, whereas MultiBit learns multi-length binary hash codes through continuous diffusion scales for cross-modal search.

papers.t: Eval4DiRec: A Unified and Systematic Evaluation Framework for Diffusion-based Recommender Systems
papers.idea: Eval4DiRec presents a modular evaluation framework for diffusion-based recommender systems. It standardizes data processing, diffusion model implementations, training schedules, and evaluation metrics across diverse recommendation settings. The benchmark assesses diffusion configurations, robustness to noise, and long-tail item performance against standard recommendation baselines.
papers.link: Both papers tackle generative architectures and tail-item performance in recommender systems. UNIQUE integrates flat quantization with generative code prediction, while Eval4DiRec benchmarks and evaluates continuous diffusion-based recommendation models.

papers.t: EvoSkillRec: Skill-Genome Evolution for Recommender Architecture Discovery
papers.idea: EvoSkillRec automates recommender architecture design by representing models as typed skill genomes. It searches across a constrained skill-space for recombining validated modules and an open-ended code-space where LLMs generate new components. An automated loop evaluates architectures, diagnoses failures, and promotes successful modules into a reusable library.
papers.link: Both papers target large-scale industrial recommender systems spanning retrieval and ranking stages. UNIQUE designs a specific unified quantization and scoring architecture, whereas EvoSkillRec uses evolutionary search and language models to discover novel modular architectures automatically.

papers.t: No Attention, No Problem: Rethinking Session-based Recommendation with Pure Convolution
papers.idea: NextConvRec uses a pure convolutional architecture for session-based recommendation without attention mechanisms. It combines convolutional positional biases with GCN-derived session structural signals, followed by depthwise and pointwise convolutions to widen the effective receptive field.
papers.link: Both works model user interaction sequences to suggest items. UNIQUE utilizes generative code prediction with target-code scoring, whereas NextConvRec discards attention and generative frameworks in favor of a purely convolutional session model.

papers.t: ColNanoVDR: Document-Free Query Distillation for Multi-Vector Visual Document Retrieval via Optimal Transport
papers.idea: ColNanoVDR distills multi-billion-parameter multi-vector query encoders into lightweight text-only students without encoding or caching document pages. It aligns student and teacher query token representations via entropic optimal transport with learned student token weights. This objective guarantees a theoretical bound on the late-interaction MaxSim score difference across unseen pages.
papers.link: Both papers study multi-vector and fine-grained representation matching for information access. UNIQUE compresses items into discrete codes for unified candidate generation and ranking, whereas ColNanoVDR compresses multi-vector document encoders via optimal transport distillation for late-interaction retrieval.

papers.t: PEAR: Progressive Evidence-Based AutoResearch for Industrial Search Systems
papers.idea: PEAR automates strategy optimization for industrial search systems using an evidence-driven agent loop. It manages hypothesis-guided states via plan-execute-evaluate-update transitions. A confidence-gated verifier ladder evaluates candidate modifications across four levels of increasing fidelity, using statistical gates before promoting candidates to expensive online tests.
papers.link: Both papers target large-scale industrial search and recommendation systems. UNIQUE introduces an algorithmic model structure unifying retrieval and ranking, while PEAR develops an automated, evidence-driven experimentation loop to optimize production systems.

papers.t: Mitigating Popularity Bias in Recommendation with Global Listwise Learning and Progressive Bi-Weighting
papers.idea: This paper presents a debiasing framework that combines an inverse propensity scored multinomial likelihood with progressive bi-weighting. It captures global listwise user preferences across all items instead of pointwise or pairwise comparisons. The bi-weighting scheme stabilizes propensity estimation and prevents over-correcting tail items during training.
papers.link: Both methods address the challenge of representing and serving long-tail items in recommendation. UNIQUE prevents tail degradation using single-layer flat quantization, while this work uses inverse propensity scoring and listwise bi-weighting over continuous collaborative filtering models.

papers.t: RenderRank: Learning to Rerank Text with Compressed Visual Tokens
papers.idea: RenderRank scores document relevance by rendering text into images and encoding them as visual tokens with a vision-language model. This compression reduces input token counts compared to text sequences while preserving document content. Training first aligns visual relevance scores with a text-based teacher model, then refines relative candidate rankings.
papers.link: Both works study two-stage candidate retrieval and scoring pipelines. UNIQUE builds an internal, target-code-aware discriminative ranker on quantized codes, whereas RenderRank scores retrieved documents by processing visually rendered text through vision-language cross-encoders.

papers.t: Signal or Noise? Modality Contribution and Cooperation in Multimodal GraphRAG
papers.idea: This paper investigates how modalities cooperate or create redundancy within multimodal GraphRAG systems. It extends a knowledge graph QA framework to track source modalities at the triple level and uses Shapley values to measure modality contribution and interaction across document visual question answering tasks.
papers.link: These papers operate in separate domains. UNIQUE builds unified generative retrieval and ranking pipelines for feeds, whereas this work evaluates modality contributions and redundancy in multimodal knowledge-graph question answering.

papers.t: Can Generative Retrievers Learn Semantic IDs Without Forgetting How to Speak?
papers.idea: Generative retrieval fine-tuning causes language models to forget their natural language capabilities. SpeakGR pairs supervised semantic identifier learning with an on-policy distillation objective against a frozen base model over text tokens. An adaptive variant dynamically scales regularization strength to mitigate language drift while maintaining retrieval accuracy.
papers.link: Both papers examine generative retrieval pipelines using discrete item identifiers. While UNIQUE replaces multi-token hierarchical codes with flat quantization to stop error propagation, SpeakGR regularizes multi-token semantic identifier training with on-policy distillation to retain general language abilities.

papers.t: Rubric-Calibrated Preferences: Cross-Query Calibration of LLM Judgments via Item Response Theory
papers.idea: Reranker evaluation suffers from sparse, coarse, or non-comparable relevance judgments across queries. The authors combine listwise Bradley-Terry tournaments with pointwise evaluations against shared binary rubrics. Item Response Theory merges these outputs onto a single cross-query scale, producing continuous relevance probabilities for nDCG calculation.
papers.link: Both papers involve ranking mechanisms, but UNIQUE deploys an online unified retrieval-ranking model, while this work focuses on offline evaluation methodology by calibrating LLM judge rubrics using Item Response Theory.

papers.t: Structured Interaction, Visual Localization, and Robust Execution for Complex Web Tasks: A Technical Report on the WebRetriever Challenge
papers.idea: The system automates web tasks by combining structured page interactions with on-demand visual perception. It uses semantic DOM representations for standard operations, falling back to grid-assisted visual localization when structured elements fail. Hierarchical context management and fault-aware multi-browser scheduling prevent context exhaustion and isolate runtime execution failures.
papers.link: These papers address distinct domains: UNIQUE develops a high-throughput feed recommendation model, whereas this report designs an agentic framework combining DOM trees and visual inputs for interactive web automation.

papers.t: GRP v0.1 Technical Report
papers.idea: GRP unifies retrieval, ranking, and alignment into a single encoder-decoder model for recommendation. It tokenizes items with vision-language Semantic IDs and integrates a multi-head prediction ranking module, which also serves as the reward model during policy optimization.
papers.link: Both systems collapse separate retrieval and ranking stages into a single unified recommendation model. UNIQUE relies on single-layer flat quantization to prevent hierarchical error propagation, while GRP generates multi-token hierarchical semantic IDs and applies a multi-head prediction head.

papers.t: Optimizing VLP-aligned Multimodal Intent Representation with Correct Visual Instantiation for Zero-Shot Composed Image Retrieval
papers.idea: This paper addresses zero-shot composed image retrieval under frozen vision-language models. It reasons about multimodal intent via language modeling and isolates visual instances in a training-free manner. These components fuse into an aligned representation to retrieve target images without triplet supervision.
papers.link: Both papers address retrieval tasks, but UNIQUE predicts quantized feed items for user profiles, whereas this work aligns vision-language representations for zero-shot composed image retrieval.

papers.t: Do Evidence-Reading Diagnostics Improve Interface Selection in Small LLM Recommenders?
papers.idea: The paper investigates whether diagnostic tests of evidence reading help choose recommendation interfaces for small language models. It evaluates selectors that dynamically switch among history-only prompting, collaborative evidence prompting, and score fusion. Diagnostic evidence-reading features fail to improve recommendation choices over observable features or a fixed validation-chosen interface.
papers.link: Both papers focus on recommendation models, but UNIQUE designs an end-to-end discrete quantization model for feed candidates, whereas this paper investigates behavioral interface selection diagnostics for small LLM-based recommenders.

papers.t: MERGE: Multi-LLM Ensemble for Retrieval via Generative Enrichment
papers.idea: MERGE enriches retrieval queries using a two-stage LLM pipeline. Multiple compact language models independently generate candidate expansions, which a larger model generatively combines into a single query. A task-grounded automatic prompt optimization loop tunes model prompts directly against downstream retrieval scores.
papers.link: Both works improve retrieval pipelines, but UNIQUE performs generative candidate retrieval via learned discrete codes, whereas MERGE performs prompt-based query expansion for classical lexical retrievers.

papers.t: Towards Semi-Automatically Comparing Keyword-Based and Semantic Search Accuracy
papers.idea: The paper presents a framework to quantitatively compare keyword-based search against semantic chat systems across different output formats. It evaluates ranking accuracy for ranked document lists alongside information completeness for conversational answers. The authors validate the method in an industrial setting by comparing Confluence search with retrieval-augmented generation.
papers.link: These papers share an evaluation and information access focus. UNIQUE introduces an industrial retrieval-ranking model, while this work develops a methodology to compare lexical search engines directly with conversational semantic chat systems.

papers.t: Generated Query Expansion Still Helps Strong Sparse Retrieval: A Controlled Study with SPLADE-v3
papers.idea: This study tests whether generated query expansion improves the strong learned sparse retriever SPLADE-v3 on scientific search. It evaluates four text generation formats alongside a structured concept graph using frozen document indices and fixed query budgets. LLM-generated vocabulary consistently improves retrieval performance across datasets when interpolated with the original query.
papers.link: Both works deal with candidate retrieval. UNIQUE rearchitects industrial feed retrieval into generative quantized code prediction, while this paper focuses on augmenting learned sparse inverted indices via LLM query expansions.

papers.t: Effective Dense Retrieval using Only In-Context Examples
papers.idea: RICE generates dense text representations from decoder-only language models without additional training. It prompts the model to produce a representative word for a query or document and takes the final hidden state as the embedding. In-context query-document examples provide a shared prompt context to align query and document representations.
papers.link: Both papers explore unified representation spaces for item retrieval. UNIQUE constructs end-to-end discrete codebooks for recommendation items, whereas RICE extracts training-free continuous text embeddings directly from LLM activations using in-context examples.

papers.t: TAGGRAPH: Tag-Augmented Graphs for Graph Retrieval of Agent Persistent Histories
papers.idea: This paper establishes a controlled evaluation framework for agent long-term memory retrieval using shared 5W-style representations. It compares localized graph traversals, diffusion via Personalized PageRank on chronological graphs, and lexical retrieval over identical notes. Experiments show graph diffusion excels on distractor-heavy histories while localized traversal or lexical baselines win on compact stores.
papers.link: These papers pursue unrelated tasks: UNIQUE optimizes large-scale user feed retrieval via discrete quantization, while TAGGRAPH benchmarks long-term memory retrieval over structured graph histories for autonomous agents.

papers.t: AdaM-Rec: Adaptive Modality Routing for Multimodal Recommendation
papers.idea: AdaM-Rec dynamically routes recommendation queries between textual and multimodal retrieval channels instead of using static fusion. It creates pseudo-queries targeting historical interactions to measure modality recall reliability for a given user context, then applies the selected strategy to retrieve and rerank candidate items.
papers.link: Both works study item retrieval and reranking in recommender systems. UNIQUE unifies retrieval and ranking into a single code-based model, while AdaM-Rec coordinates a multi-stage pipeline by dynamically routing queries between textual and multimodal channels.

papers.t: Re-ranking and Late Interaction Drive Retrieval Quality: A Controlled Comparison of RAG Strategies for Scientific Question Answering
papers.idea: The paper presents a controlled comparison of retrieval-augmented generation strategies for scientific question answering. It tests methods including query expansion, late interaction, reranking, and agentic workflows using an LLM-as-a-judge evaluation setup. The analysis shows that re-ranking and late interaction mechanisms dominate retrieval quality gains.
papers.link: Both papers examine the interplay between retrieval and subsequent ranking stages. UNIQUE unifies candidate retrieval and ranking in a single quantized recommender, while this study benchmarks multi-stage retrieval, reranking, and late-interaction strategies for text-based RAG.

papers.t: Exploring Forum Post Retrieval with Generative Modeling
papers.idea: This paper adapts autoregressive generative recommendation to Facebook Forum posts under data sparsity. It reuses hierarchical semantic IDs pre-trained on Facebook Feed data and trains a 3B-parameter language model on Facebook Groups engagement histories. The model generates semantic tokens for candidate posts directly from user interaction prompts.
papers.link: Both papers develop generative recommendation systems for feed environments. UNIQUE avoids hierarchical semantic IDs in favor of single-layer flat quantization, whereas this work directly applies hierarchical semantic IDs trained via RQ-VAE to post retrieval.

papers.t: PatchHolmes: Agentic Patch Retrieval via Listwise Selection
papers.idea: PatchHolmes identifies the git commit fixing a known vulnerability using a two-stage approach. A hybrid retriever first selects the top-100 candidate commits, after which an LLM agent inspects candidate diffs listwise using budgeted tools to select the best commit.
papers.link: These papers address distinct domains; UNIQUE targets large-scale feed item recommendation, while PatchHolmes designs a two-stage agentic workflow to retrieve and inspect code commits for security vulnerabilities.

papers.t: SkillSeek: Revisiting Agent Skill Retrieval at Marketplace Scale
papers.idea: SkillSeek replaces LLM-mediated agent skill search with a deterministic information retrieval pipeline. It uses a BGE-base bi-encoder and a small cross-encoder exposed through an MCP server interface. This achieves task pass rates comparable to iterative LLM loops on SkillsBench while cutting total token costs in half.
papers.link: Both papers explore retrieval-and-ranking systems. UNIQUE develops a generative recommendation model over quantized items, whereas SkillSeek implements a deterministic bi-encoder and cross-encoder pipeline for agent skill lookup.

papers.t: Text-Video Retrieval via Multi-Dimensional Saliency Assessment and Granularity-Aware Query Decomposition
papers.idea: MMTI addresses visual redundancy and multi-level semantic alignment in text-video retrieval. A key feature selection mechanism selects informative frames and patches using multi-dimensional saliency and learnable importance scores. A dynamic gating module then decomposes text queries into sentence, frame, and patch representations for multi-grained alignment.
papers.link: Both papers work on candidate retrieval problems, but UNIQUE optimizes sequential feed recommendation using vector quantization, whereas MMTI focuses on cross-modal text-to-video alignment via dynamic token gating.

papers.t: When LLM-Inferred User Context Adds Value in Production Streaming Recommendation
papers.idea: The paper investigates using large language models to infer latent user context from consumption histories for streaming recommendation. It evaluates holistic and attention-fused temporal representations against conventional embedding centroids on production data. The study identifies specific user consumption regimes where language-model-derived summaries improve recommendation performance.
papers.link: Both works aim to improve industrial streaming recommendation through user sequence modeling. UNIQUE replaces multi-stage pipelines with flat quantization and generative scoring, whereas this work evaluates LLM-derived textual contexts within traditional embedding-based recommenders.

papers.t: RouteRec: Behavior-Guided Sparse Routing for Sequential Recommendation
papers.idea: RouteRec routes sequential recommendation inputs through a mixture of experts based on behavioral cues. It derives cues covering tempo, focus, memory, and popularity from session logs to guide multi-scope expert allocation without requiring explicit routing labels.
papers.link: Both papers investigate sequential recommendation systems. UNIQUE combines generative retrieval and discriminative ranking via flat quantization, while RouteRec routes user behavior sequences through dynamic mixtures of experts.

papers.t: Routing Between Generative and Collaborative User Profiles: A Serving-Time Gate for Controllable Novelty
papers.idea: A learned routing gate dynamically chooses between collaborative sequential recommenders and LLM-generated profile models for individual users at serving time. The model uses historical interactions and representations to balance recommendation novelty against relevance loss. Varying the gate threshold provides a controllable trade-off frontier.
papers.link: Both papers study generative paradigms in recommendation. UNIQUE builds a unified quantized pipeline for feed delivery, while this paper dynamically arbitrates between classical collaborative models and LLM generative profile models to control recommendation novelty.

papers.t: Learning Multiresolution Relevance for Hierarchical Generative Retrieval
papers.idea: Generative retrieval with semantic identifiers resolves queries hierarchically, but standard full-path training ignores local relevance splits. RARS aggregates document relevance across identifier prefixes to define consistent conditional distributions at each depth. It trains a prefix-conditioned predictor to allocate relevance among sibling branches, discarding the predictor at test time to keep standard autoregressive decoding.
papers.link: Both papers tackle identifier design in generative retrieval. UNIQUE discards hierarchical codes entirely to prevent cascading errors via flat quantization, whereas RARS retains hierarchical IDs and addresses branching errors by supervising prefix-level relevance splits.

papers.t: Residual Trajectory Distillation for Generative Retrieval
papers.idea: Generative retrieval models map queries to discrete semantic IDs (SIDs) built using residual quantization, but standard training discards the continuous residual trajectories. ResTD uses the frozen residual indexer as a process teacher to distill codeword preferences into the decoder hidden states. This transfer preserves geometric indexing information across quantization levels without modifying the underlying retrieval index.
papers.link: Both works address generative retrieval using vector quantization. UNIQUE replaces residual multi-code schemes with a single flat quantization layer to reduce errors, while ResTD keeps multi-step residual quantization and distills intermediate continuous trajectory features into the generative decoder.

papers.t: Generative End-to-end Ad Retrieval at Douyin
papers.idea: GEAR formulates ad retrieval as an end-to-end discrete generative pipeline. It introduces BasisVQ to prevent codebook collapse by reparameterizing codes with an orthogonal basis. An integrated context-conditioned reranking head then resolves item token collisions during generation.
papers.link: Both systems address industrial candidate generation using generative vector quantization. UNIQUE uses feedback-aware single-layer flat quantization with a discriminative scoring head, whereas Douyin's GEAR uses multi-stage residual codes stabilized by BasisVQ and an item collision reranking head.

papers.t: When the Label Ignores the Request: Auditing Policy-Selected Targets in Synthetic Conversational Music Recommendation
papers.idea: Synthetic conversational recommendation benchmarks often assign ground-truth targets based on what a simulated recommender chose rather than what the user requested. This paper audits synthetic dialogues where users specify exact track titles, revealing frequent label divergence. It evaluates retraining systems on targets aligned directly with explicit user requests.
papers.link: Both papers focus on item recommendation accuracy. UNIQUE designs a model architecture for large-scale feeds, while this paper audits synthetic dialogue benchmarks to highlight discrepancies between user requests and ground-truth recommendation labels.

papers.t: KUAISHOU Explorer LLM-Rec Challenge 2026: Reasoning Generative Recommendation
papers.idea: This report presents the KUAISHOU Explorer LLM-Rec Challenge 2026 on reasoning generative recommendation. The competition evaluates unified language models that map item semantic IDs and natural language to perform user interest reasoning and item prediction. The authors release pretrained models, interaction sequences, chain-of-thought fine-tuning data, and benchmarks across four task categories.
papers.link: Both works explore generative recommendation using discrete item tokens. UNIQUE avoids hierarchical multi-token sequences via flat quantization, while the Kuaishou benchmark relies on multi-granularity semantic IDs paired with chain-of-thought reasoning.

papers.t: Decision-Oriented Recommendation Reranking: An Empirical Study of Jev
papers.idea: This paper evaluates Jev, a decision-oriented model, for personalized recommendation reranking on controlled candidate sets from Amazon Reviews. It compares Jev against recommendation-specific models and Qwen2.5 rerankers. Results analyze the quality-latency trade-offs across different candidate list sizes.
papers.link: Both papers examine the ranking component of recommendation pipelines. UNIQUE merges retrieval and ranking into a single end-to-end framework, whereas this study evaluates latency and quality trade-offs of standalone reranking models over pre-filtered candidate sets.

papers.t: On-Device Commercial Intent Retrieval Under Size, Latency, and Privacy Constraints: A 3 MiB Retrieval System with Typed Egress Boundaries
papers.idea: An on-device retrieval pipeline infers commercial intent over a 6,020-leaf taxonomy without sending raw text, embeddings, or persistent identifiers to servers. It distills a Korean sentence transformer into a 4-bit static embedding table operating under 3 MiB and 20 ms latency. A typed egress boundary and federated layer prevent unauthorized identifier or representation leakage.
papers.link: Both works utilize vector quantization to compress representations for low-latency retrieval. UNIQUE trains a centralized server system with flat codes for feed feeds, while this work quantizes sentence embeddings into 4-bit static tables to perform private intent classification directly on user devices.

papers.t: System Attribution in LLM Brand Recommendations: Single Responses Identify the System, Aggregated Brand Profiles Do Not Transfer
papers.idea: This paper investigates whether AI brand recommendation profiles reflect underlying language model systems. Character n-gram classifiers identify the generating system from single responses with over 97% accuracy using surface formatting alone. In contrast, aggregated brand-level behavioral metrics fail to transfer across query domains due to domain and collection harness confounding.
papers.link: These papers differ fundamentally in topic: UNIQUE implements an industrial recommendation engine, while this paper studies system attribution and brand prominence patterns in LLM response text.

papers.t: A Shared Taste for Model-Written Text: The Generator-by-Selector Matrices of "AI-AI Bias" Show No Detectable Own-Model Premium
papers.idea: The paper re-analyzes published generator-by-selector experimental data to test whether large language models prefer their own generated text. It fits a two-way fixed-effects model across multiple domains and uses permutation tests. The analysis reveals no detectable own-model premium, showing models instead share general preferences for specific machine-written text.
papers.link: These works focus on different domains; UNIQUE develops an end-to-end model for feed recommendation, whereas this paper investigates whether LLMs exhibit self-preference bias when evaluating model-generated text.

papers.t: Comparison of Common Crawl News & GDELT
papers.idea: This paper analyzes and compares the content and geographic coverage of Common Crawl News and GDELT. It evaluates how each repository gathers sources, contrasting GDELT's structured multi-media event tracking with Common Crawl's raw web-crawled text data. The analysis shows significant variations in where each dataset sources its global news.
papers.link: These papers address unrelated domains. UNIQUE presents a generative retrieval and ranking architecture for feeds, whereas this work evaluates news coverage differences between Common Crawl and GDELT.

papers.t: CANOPY: Adaptive-Granularity Evidence Compression for Multimodal RAG
papers.idea: Retrieved multimodal items are structured into hierarchical trees of varying granularities. A fine-tuned node encoder scores regions against the query, and parent-relative comparison selects relevant sub-regions without LLM pruning. An iterative critic triggers follow-up retrieval when accumulated evidence is insufficient to answer the query.
papers.link: Both systems optimize information retrieval and downstream scoring. UNIQUE targets feed recommendation using discrete code generation, while CANOPY compresses visual evidence into hierarchical trees for multimodal retrieval-augmented generation.

papers.t: RPTune: Learned Context Curation for LLM Catalog Search
papers.idea: RPTune addresses long-context catalog search for small businesses without multi-stage retrieval pipelines. An encoder-reorganizer prunes and positions products using downstream LLM feedback to counter position bias. The LLM is then post-trained on these curated contexts via reinforcement learning with synthetic, catalog-grounded supervision.
papers.link: Both works challenge standard multi-stage search pipelines for catalog items. UNIQUE uses flat discrete quantization to handle retrieval and ranking together, while RPTune feeds full product catalogs into long-context LLMs via learned reorganizers.

papers.t: Do Multilingual Encoders Produce Language-Consistent Semantic IDs?
papers.idea: Multilingual encoders and residual quantizers often fail to assign consistent Semantic IDs to translated product listings. The authors measure how translation displacement alters discrete code sequences across English, Spanish, and Japanese. They find that balancing the quantizer fitting mixture makes codebook use more uniform but actually reduces prefix agreement across languages.
papers.link: Both papers evaluate discrete semantic identifiers in retrieval pipelines. UNIQUE switches from hierarchical semantic IDs to flat quantization to bypass indexing bottlenecks, while this paper evaluates how multilingual representations compromise the stability of residual semantic IDs across languages.

papers.t: Learning to structure data from user-generated thematic corpora
papers.idea: The paper presents an iterative framework to discover domain-specific attributes from thematic corpora without predefined ontologies. Language models propose candidate attributes, consolidate semantic overlaps, and assign structural types. The pipeline produces stable schemas for automated extraction across user-generated documents.
papers.link: These papers address distinct problems; UNIQUE focuses on user item retrieval and ranking, whereas this paper extracts domain-specific attribute schemas from unstructured social text.

papers.t: From Rules to Neural Graphs: Scalable Structured Prediction for Patent Prior Art Search
papers.idea: This paper converts patent documents into structured invention graphs for retrieval using a neural parser. It modifies biaffine attention with a sliding window to predict graph edges in linear time over long texts. The model is trained by distilling rules from one million parsed documents and integrates into a downstream Graph Transformer.
papers.link: Both papers deal with candidate retrieval over structured representations. UNIQUE uses flat quantized codes for recommendation, whereas this work constructs graph structures via sliding-window attention for patent document retrieval.

papers.t: AgentWebRec: Compact Evidence Fusion over the Agent Web for Personalized Recommendation
papers.idea: AgentWebRec reorganizes recommendation into an interaction among user agents, platform agents, and peer agents. A user agent enhances candidate item semantics via platform queries, retrieves relevant private memories, and collaborates across an agent web using confidence gating to rank recommendations.
papers.link: Both works focus on personalized recommendation. UNIQUE unifies candidate selection into a single neural model with discrete codes, whereas AgentWebRec delegates personalization to multi-agent interactions across user, platform, and peer modules.

papers.t: Optimizing Effective Training Time for Large-Scale Recommendation Systems
papers.idea: This paper measures accelerator overheads across the full training lifecycle of large recommendation models using an Effective Training Time (ETT%) metric. The framework decomposes non-training wall time into specific infrastructure components and failure recoveries. Targeted optimizations, including compilation caching, asynchronous checkpointing, and initialization overlapping, recover lost GPU capacity across clusters.
papers.link: Both papers address computational efficiency in production recommendation systems. UNIQUE focuses on algorithmic unification of retrieval and ranking, whereas this work optimizes GPU cluster training throughput via checkpointing and compilation improvements.

papers.t: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
papers.idea: Combines a pre-trained sequence-to-sequence model with a dense passage retriever to generate text grounded in retrieved documents.
papers.link: This foundation paper introduces retrieval-augmented generation combining passage retrieval with generative sequence prediction. UNIQUE adapts the generative retrieval paradigm to industrial feeds, replacing dual-encoder retrieval with unified flat quantization and generative scoring.

papers.t: Qwen3 Embedding: Advancing Text Embedding and Reranking Through Foundation Models
papers.idea: Uses foundation language models to produce text embeddings and reranking scores for retrieval tasks.
papers.link: Both systems perform retrieval and ranking, but Qwen3 relies on foundation language models for dense text embeddings and cross-encoder scores, whereas UNIQUE uses generative code prediction and discriminative ranking over quantized item codes.

papers.t: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
papers.idea: Applies self-attention mechanisms to a user's past interaction sequence to predict the next item.
papers.link: UNIQUE builds on self-attentive sequence modeling from SASRec to capture historical user interactions, but extends the framework to directly generate quantized item codes and unify retrieval with ranking.

papers.t: The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond
papers.v: Foundations and Trends in Information Retrieval
papers.idea: Surveys and formalizes the probabilistic relevance framework and term-weighting formulas of the BM25 retrieval model.
papers.link: BM25 serves as an inverted-index lexical matching heuristic for document text, whereas UNIQUE performs end-to-end feed recommendation via learnable flat vector quantization and unified generative-discriminative scoring.

papers.t: Recommender Systems with Generative Retrieval
papers.idea: Formulates recommendation as generating semantic identifiers directly using a sequence-to-sequence model.
papers.link: Both formulate item retrieval as generating discrete semantic identifiers; however, UNIQUE replaces multi-level hierarchical identifiers with single-layer flat quantization to prevent error propagation and integrates a target-code-aware ranking stage.

papers.t: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
papers.idea: Uses a dual-encoder architecture over text passages to map queries and documents into dense vectors for retrieval.
papers.link: DPR uses dual encoders and inner-product search over continuous text embeddings, while UNIQUE replaces dual-encoder retrieval with autoregressive code generation over discrete quantized representations.

papers.t: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
papers.idea: Modifies pre-trained BERT networks with siamese and triplet structures to produce semantically meaningful sentence embeddings.
papers.link: Sentence-BERT derives continuous semantic sentence vectors using siamese networks, whereas UNIQUE focuses on discrete quantization of user-item interaction signals for joint feed retrieval and ranking.

papers.t: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
papers.idea: Computes token-level vector representations via BERT and evaluates query-document relevance through late interaction with a MaxSim operator.
papers.link: ColBERT retains fine-grained token representations and computes relevance via late interaction MaxSim, while UNIQUE compresses item spaces into discrete codes for unified generative candidate retrieval.

papers.t: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
papers.idea: Employs a bidirectional transformer encoder with a cloze task to model user behavior sequences for recommendation.
papers.link: UNIQUE takes the concept of transformer-based sequential behavior modeling from BERT4Rec, but shifts from bidirectional masked item prediction to autoregressive generative retrieval paired with unified ranking.

papers.t: BGE M3-Embedding: Multi-Lingual, Multi-Functionality, Multi-Granularity Text Embeddings Through Self-Knowledge Distillation
papers.idea: Trains an embedding model supporting dense, multi-vector, and sparse retrieval across multiple languages and granularities.
papers.link: BGE M3 targets multi-granularity multilingual dense and sparse text retrieval, whereas UNIQUE targets industrial feed recommendation via quantized discrete code generation and CTR scoring.

papers.t: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
papers.idea: Interleaves reasoning traces and task-specific action execution within large language models to interact with external environments.
papers.link: ReAct coordinates reasoning traces and tool-use actions in language agents, whereas UNIQUE is a specialized recommender architecture combining quantized generative candidate retrieval with discriminative scoring.

papers.t: BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of Information Retrieval Models
papers.idea: Provides a heterogeneous benchmark across multiple domains and tasks to evaluate information retrieval systems in zero-shot settings.
papers.link: BEIR establishes zero-shot text retrieval benchmarks across heterogeneous NLP domains, whereas UNIQUE focuses on industrial feed recommendation evaluated on user interaction logs.

papers.t: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
papers.idea: Trains language models to output reflection tokens that control when to retrieve and evaluate retrieved passage relevance and generation quality.
papers.link: Self-RAG trains language models to output reflection tokens for adaptive passage retrieval, whereas UNIQUE uses generated discrete codes directly as item candidates within an integrated retrieval-and-ranking pipeline.

papers.t: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
papers.idea: Proposes a non-softmax sequential transducer architecture with point-wise activation and temporal gating for large-scale recommendation sequences.
papers.link: Both scale generative sequential recommendation to industrial workloads, but UNIQUE focuses on unifying retrieval and ranking through flat vector quantization rather than non-softmax sequential transducer architectures.

papers.t: Reciprocal Rank Fusion Outperforms Condorcet and Individual Rank Learning Methods
papers.idea: Combines rankings from multiple retrieval systems using the sum of reciprocal ranks without requiring score calibration.
papers.link: RRF combines disparate rank lists via rank-score aggregation heuristics, whereas UNIQUE integrates candidate retrieval and ranking internally within a single parameterized neural network.

papers.t: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
papers.idea: Surveys the development of retrieval-augmented generation paradigms, architectures, components, and evaluation methods for large language models.
papers.link: This survey analyzes retrieval-augmented text generation methods in large language models, whereas UNIQUE uses generative modeling as a mechanism to retrieve and rank items in feed recommendation.

papers.t: ColBERTv2: Effective and Efficient Retrieval via Lightweight Late Interaction
papers.idea: Pairs late interaction retrieval with residual vector compression and supervision from cross-encoders to reduce index size and computation.
papers.link: ColBERTv2 compresses multi-vector text indices using residual quantization for passage search, while UNIQUE applies feedback-aware flat vector quantization to map items into discrete identifiers for generative recommendation.

papers.t: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
papers.idea: Introduces bidirectional pre-training for transformers using masked language modeling and next-sentence prediction.
papers.link: UNIQUE adopts the multi-head self-attention mechanisms popularized by BERT to encode user behavior histories, adapting them for autoregressive code generation.

papers.t: Session-based Recommendations with Recurrent Neural Networks
papers.idea: Adapts gated recurrent units to model sequential user interactions in short, anonymous browsing sessions.
papers.link: GRU4Rec introduced sequential interaction modeling for recommendations, which UNIQUE advances using transformer architectures, discrete quantization, and unified retrieval-ranking stages.

papers.t: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
papers.idea: Freezes pre-trained model weights and injects trainable rank-decomposition matrices into transformer layers to reduce fine-tuning parameters.
papers.link: LoRA provides parameter-efficient adaptation for frozen transformer weights, whereas UNIQUE modifies the model architecture and indexing structure via quantized discrete code generation.

papers.t: GPT-4 Technical Report
papers.idea: This report describes the architecture, training process, and multimodal capabilities of GPT-4.
papers.link: GPT-4 is a general-purpose multimodal foundation model, whereas UNIQUE is a domain-specific architecture designed to optimize candidate retrieval and ranking in industrial feed recommendation.

papers.t: Passage Re-ranking with BERT
papers.idea: The paper adapts pretrained BERT models as neural rerankers for passage retrieval.
papers.link: Passage Re-ranking with BERT isolates the reranking step in a multi-stage search pipeline, while UNIQUE integrates candidate generation and discriminative ranking within a unified quantized model.

papers.t: The MovieLens Datasets: History and Context
papers.idea: This paper documents the creation, usage, and structure of the MovieLens recommendation benchmark datasets.
papers.link: MovieLens provides academic benchmark datasets for collaborative filtering, whereas UNIQUE addresses large-scale multi-stage feed recommendation pipelines handling industrial traffic.

papers.t: C-Pack: Packed Resources for General Chinese Embeddings
papers.idea: The authors introduce resources, benchmarks, and the BGE embedding and reranking models for text retrieval.
papers.link: C-Pack develops bi-encoder and cross-encoder models for general text search, whereas UNIQUE designs unified generative retrieval and discriminative ranking for item recommendation.

papers.t: Qwen3 Technical Report
papers.idea: This report details the architectural improvements and training methods of the Qwen3 large language model family.
papers.link: Qwen3 details foundation model scaling and pre-training methodologies, whereas UNIQUE addresses efficiency and error propagation in recommender systems via end-to-end vector quantization.

papers.t: Improving Text Embeddings with Large Language Models
papers.idea: This work uses synthetic data generation and large language models to train general-purpose dense text embeddings.
papers.link: This work synthesizes training data to optimize continuous dense text embeddings, whereas UNIQUE learns discrete item quantization directly from recommendation user feedback.

papers.t: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
papers.idea: The paper proposes FLARE, a method that triggers external information retrieval dynamically based on low-confidence token predictions during text generation.
papers.link: FLARE triggers text retrieval dynamically based on confidence tokens during generation, whereas UNIQUE uses generative prediction of discrete codes as the retrieval mechanism itself.

papers.t: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
papers.idea: The authors show that language models access information placed at the start or end of long input contexts more accurately than information in the middle.
papers.link: Lost in the Middle identifies context-position biases in language models, while UNIQUE addresses error propagation and long-tail coverage in recommender systems by moving to flat quantization.

papers.t: HotpotQA: A Dataset for Diverse, Explainable Multi-Hop Question Answering
papers.idea: The authors present a question-answering dataset that requires reasoning across multiple documents and supplies sentence-level supporting facts.
papers.link: HotpotQA evaluates multi-hop question answering across text corpora, whereas UNIQUE focuses on next-item click-through rate prediction and candidate retrieval in recommendation feeds.

papers.t: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
papers.idea: The authors study using strong large language models as automated judges to evaluate conversational assistants.
papers.link: This paper evaluates LLM-based judges for conversational chat benchmarks, while UNIQUE targets user engagement metrics such as click-through rate in feed recommendations.

papers.t: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
papers.idea: This paper presents the Adam optimization algorithm, which computes adaptive learning rates from estimates of first and second gradient moments.
papers.link: UNIQUE relies on gradient-based optimizers like Adam to train its end-to-end vector quantization, retrieval, and ranking modules.

papers.t: Deep Neural Networks for YouTube Recommendations
papers.idea: The paper introduces a two-stage deep learning architecture that separates candidate generation from ranking for large-scale video recommendations.
papers.link: YouTube Recommendations established the canonical decoupled two-stage paradigm separating candidate retrieval and ranking, which UNIQUE unifies into a single framework.

papers.t: Cumulated Gain-Based Evaluation of IR Techniques
papers.idea: The paper introduces Discounted Cumulative Gain and Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain to evaluate search results with graded relevance.
papers.link: UNIQUE relies on ranking metrics like NDCG defined in this work to evaluate the accuracy of its combined retrieval and ranking outputs.

papers.t: Image-Based Recommendations on Styles and Substitutes
papers.idea: The paper develops methods to predict related items using visual and text features, releasing the Amazon Review dataset collections.
papers.link: This work explores visual-textual features and item co-occurrence graphs, whereas UNIQUE unifies user sequence modeling, discrete candidate generation, and click-through rate ranking.
