papers.t: Neural Collaborative Filtering
papers.idea: The authors replace traditional matrix factorization dot products with neural network architectures to capture non-linear user-item interactions.
papers.link: NCF replaces inner products with non-linear neural interactions for collaborative filtering, while UNIQUE frames recommendation as autoregressive generation over quantized item codes coupled with discriminative scoring.

papers.t: BRIGHT: A Realistic and Challenging Benchmark for Reasoning-Intensive Retrieval
papers.idea: The authors introduce a benchmark to evaluate information retrieval systems on queries that require multi-step logical, mathematical, or coding reasoning.
papers.link: BRIGHT assesses complex reasoning for information retrieval, whereas UNIQUE targets high-throughput feed recommendations using single-layer flat quantization.

papers.t: Transformer Memory as a Differentiable Search Index
papers.idea: The authors propose the Differentiable Search Index, which directly maps query text to document identifiers within a single sequence-to-sequence model.
papers.link: DSI pioneered generative retrieval by mapping queries directly to document identifiers, a concept UNIQUE adapts to recommendations while using flat quantization and appending a target-code-aware ranking head.

papers.t: Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction
papers.idea: The authors present the Deep Interest Network, which uses local activation units to capture user interests from historical behaviors relevant to a target candidate item.
papers.link: DIN uses target-aware attention for candidate ranking, a principle UNIQUE incorporates into its target-code-aware discriminative scoring head after generating candidate codes.

papers.t: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
papers.idea: The authors combine knowledge graphs and modular community detection with language models to support global summarization across text corpora.
papers.link: Graph RAG constructs knowledge graphs for text summarization, whereas UNIQUE focuses on behavioral user logs and discrete item quantization for feed recommendation.

papers.t: Is ChatGPT Good at Search? Investigating Large Language Models as Re-Ranking Agents
papers.idea: This paper evaluates instructional large language models as zero-shot listwise document rerankers via permutation generation.
papers.link: RankGPT applies prompted autoregressive LLMs to sort text passages listwise, whereas UNIQUE trains custom quantized networks to output candidate codes and discriminative scores directly.

papers.t: LightGCN: Simplifying and Powering Graph Convolution Network for Recommendation
papers.idea: This paper simplifies graph convolution for collaborative filtering by removing non-linear feature transformations and weight matrices, keeping only neighborhood aggregation.
papers.link: LightGCN computes user and item embeddings through linear neighborhood aggregation on graphs, while UNIQUE models sequential user interactions using transformer architectures and discrete quantization.

papers.t: Recommendation as Language Processing (RLP): A Unified Pretrain, Personalized Prompt & Predict Paradigm (P5)
papers.idea: This paper frames multiple recommendation tasks as conditional natural language generation using personalized prompts and unified sequence-to-sequence language models.
papers.link: P5 treats diverse recommendation problems as natural language generation via text prompts, whereas UNIQUE focuses specifically on unifying retrieval and CTR ranking using specialized flat-quantized codes.

papers.t: Text Embeddings by Weakly-Supervised Contrastive Pre-training
papers.idea: This paper trains dense text embeddings using contrastive learning over large-scale, weakly supervised text pairs gathered from web sources.
papers.link: This paper trains dual-encoder text representations using contrastive loss, whereas UNIQUE sidesteps bi-encoder dot-product search by generating discrete quantized item IDs.

papers.t: ColPali: Efficient Document Retrieval with Vision Language Models
papers.idea: This paper applies late-interaction multi-vector matching to document image patches using vision-language models, bypassing optical character recognition for visual document retrieval.
papers.link: ColPali uses vision-language late interaction for visual document retrieval, whereas UNIQUE generates discrete item tokens from sequential user logs for recommender systems.

papers.t: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
papers.idea: This paper introduces a standardized benchmark to evaluate text embedding models across diverse languages and diverse tasks including retrieval, classification, and clustering.
papers.link: MTEB evaluates dense embedding representations across textual tasks, while UNIQUE is evaluated on sequential recommendation and ranking performance in feed systems.

papers.t: Approximate Nearest Neighbor Negative Contrastive Learning for Dense Text Retrieval
papers.idea: This paper samples hard negatives for dense retrievers asynchronously from an updated approximate nearest neighbor index during contrastive training.
papers.link: ANCE focuses on hard-negative mining for bi-encoder approximate nearest neighbor search, whereas UNIQUE eliminates the separate approximate nearest neighbor index by generating discrete item codes directly.

papers.t: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels
papers.idea: This paper generates hypothetical document responses with a language model and uses an unsupervised retriever to match them against candidate passages in zero-shot retrieval.
papers.link: HyDE expands zero-shot text queries using generated hypothetical documents, while UNIQUE generates discrete item tokens directly to serve as retrieved recommendation candidates.

papers.t: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
papers.idea: This paper introduces Group Relative Policy Optimization, an algorithm that optimizes language model policies by normalizing rewards across multiple completions of the same prompt without an explicit critic network.
papers.link: DeepSeekMath introduces policy-gradient reinforcement learning methods for mathematical reasoning, whereas UNIQUE focuses on supervised generative retrieval and discriminative ranking for feeds.

papers.t: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
papers.idea: This paper trains dual image and text encoders by maximizing cosine similarity between paired images and captions with a contrastive loss over web-scale data.
papers.link: CLIP aligns image and text modalities into a joint continuous embedding space, while UNIQUE designs discrete, feedback-aware quantized codes for feed recommendation items.

papers.t: Attention Is All You Need
papers.idea: This paper introduces the Transformer architecture, replacing recurrent and convolutional sequence models entirely with multi-head self-attention mechanisms.
papers.link: UNIQUE utilizes the self-attention transformer architecture introduced in this paper as the backbone for encoding user histories and generating item codes.

papers.t: Learnable Item Tokenization for Generative Recommendation
papers.idea: This paper introduces a learned item tokenization framework that combines collaborative filtering signals and semantic representations through residual vector quantization for generative recommendation.
papers.link: Both methods tokenize items into discrete semantic identifiers for generative recommendation; however, UNIQUE replaces multi-level residual quantization with single-layer flat quantization to prevent hierarchical error propagation.

papers.t: ReasonIR: Training Retrievers for Reasoning Tasks
papers.idea: This paper constructs training data and methods specifically to teach dense retrieval models how to find relevant context for complex multi-step reasoning problems.
papers.link: ReasonIR fine-tunes dense bi-encoders specifically for reasoning-intensive document retrieval. In contrast, UNIQUE targets feed recommendation by replacing dense text search with discrete quantization codes for combined retrieval and ranking.

papers.t: DCN V2: Improved Deep & Cross Network and Practical Lessons for Web-scale Learning to Rank Systems
papers.idea: This paper proposes improved cross layers with low-rank or mixture-of-experts matrix multiplications to capture explicit feature crosses in web-scale click-through rate prediction.
papers.link: DCN V2 designs explicit feature cross layers for the discriminative ranking stage of recommendation funnels. UNIQUE instead consolidates retrieval and ranking into a single network using generative code generation paired with discriminative scoring.

papers.t: Qwen2.5-VL Technical Report
papers.idea: This report details large vision-language models trained to process arbitrary image and video resolutions through native dynamic patch representations and joint multimodal reasoning.
papers.link: Qwen2.5-VL develops native multimodal vision-language models for image and video comprehension. UNIQUE focuses entirely on user-item interaction histories and quantized item identifiers within industrial recommendation.

papers.t: Atlas: Few-shot Learning with Retrieval Augmented Language Models
papers.idea: This paper pre-trains and fine-tunes language models together with dense retrievers end-to-end, enabling few-shot question answering and knowledge-intensive task solving.
papers.link: Atlas trains language models jointly with dense document retrievers for knowledge-intensive question answering. UNIQUE operates on user feed recommendations, using quantized discrete codes rather than dense passage retrieval.

papers.t: Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Knowledge-Intensive Multi-Step Questions
papers.idea: This paper alternates between generating step-by-step chain-of-thought sentences and retrieving new supporting documents to answer complex multi-hop questions.
papers.link: This paper coordinates multi-hop question answering by interleaving text generation with iterative document retrieval. UNIQUE avoids multi-hop text reasoning, focusing instead on single-step item candidate generation and ranking via quantized codes.

papers.t: Representation Learning with Contrastive Predictive Coding
papers.a: van den Oord, Li, and Vinyals
papers.idea: This paper proposes Contrastive Predictive Coding and the InfoNCE loss to extract representations from high-dimensional signals by predicting future states against negative candidates.
papers.link: UNIQUE draws directly on the contrastive predictive coding and InfoNCE loss introduced in this paper to optimize code-level representations against negative samples. However, UNIQUE specializes these objectives for discrete item quantization rather than continuous representation learning.

papers.t: Overview of the TREC 2020 Deep Learning Track
papers.idea: This paper reports the setup, collection, and evaluation results of the TREC Deep Learning track benchmark using MS MARCO queries and dense human relevance assessments.
papers.link: This paper establishes an offline benchmark for text retrieval and passage ranking over MS MARCO data. UNIQUE targets industrial feed recommendation engines evaluated on user engagement logs.

papers.t: SPLADE: Sparse Lexical and Expansion Model for First Stage Ranking
papers.idea: This paper learns sparse query and document representations over the full vocabulary using masked language models and sparsity regularizers for inverted index retrieval.
papers.link: SPLADE performs lexical expansion for inverted index retrieval in document search. UNIQUE addresses feed recommendation by generating discrete quantization codes for candidate retrieval without lexical inverted indexes.

papers.t: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
papers.idea: This paper constructs a personalized PageRank indexing framework over entity-relation knowledge graphs derived from texts to support associative retrieval for large language models.
papers.link: HippoRAG builds knowledge graph memory structures for associative text retrieval in language models. UNIQUE handles feed recommendation and indexes candidate items directly through feedback-aware discrete quantization codes.

papers.t: NV-Embed: Improved Techniques for Training LLMs as Generalist Embedding Models
papers.idea: Introduces architectural and training methods, such as latent-attention pooling and multi-stage fine-tuning, to adapt decoder-only large language models into general-purpose text embedding models.
papers.link: NV-Embed develops architecture recipes for decoder-only dense text embeddings. UNIQUE differs by dispensing with dense bi-encoder text embeddings, using discrete generative codes for retrieval.

papers.t: Autoregressive Image Generation using Residual Quantization
papers.idea: Presents residual-quantized variational autoencoders (RQ-VAE) to discretize high-dimensional representations into hierarchical discrete code sequences for autoregressive modeling.
papers.link: RQ-VAE provides the hierarchical discrete code formulation commonly adapted into semantic identifiers for generative recommenders. UNIQUE explicitly moves away from RQ-VAE's hierarchical residual codes, adopting a flat single-layer quantization to prevent error propagation.

papers.t: Adapting Large Language Models by Integrating Collaborative Semantics for Recommendation
papers.idea: Proposes methods to integrate collaborative filtering signals with semantic representations in large language models for generative recommendation.
papers.link: This paper incorporates collaborative signals into language models using hierarchical semantic identifiers for generative recommendation. UNIQUE shares the goal of collaborative generative recommendation, but substitutes hierarchical identifiers with flat feedback-aware quantization.

papers.t: OneRec: Unifying Retrieve and Rank with Generative Recommender and Iterative Preference Alignment
papers.idea: Unifies candidate retrieval and ranking in recommender systems into a single generative model using discrete item identifiers and iterative preference alignment.
papers.link: OneRec unifies retrieval and ranking into a generative model using discrete item identifiers and iterative preference alignment. UNIQUE targets the exact same unified problem, but critiques hierarchical identifiers and introduces a flat single-layer quantization framework to resolve error propagation.

papers.t: Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models through Question Complexity
papers.idea: Routes queries to different retrieval strategies by classifying user question complexity to balance accuracy and retrieval overhead.
papers.link: Adaptive-RAG routes input questions to varying retrieval pipelines based on query complexity. UNIQUE deals with feed recommendation, routing all items through a single quantized retrieval and ranking pipeline.

papers.t: LONGER: Scaling Up Long Sequence Modeling in Industrial Recommenders
papers.idea: Proposes an efficient attention and hierarchical compression architecture to scale sequence modeling over extremely long user histories in industrial recommender systems.
papers.link: LONGER optimizes attention mechanisms to scale long-sequence user modeling in recommendation. UNIQUE also processes user interaction histories, but focuses on unifying the retrieval and ranking stages through discrete quantization.

papers.t: Make It Long, Keep It Fast: End-to-End 10k-Sequence Modeling at Billion Scale on Douyin
papers.idea: Scales end-to-end user sequence modeling up to 10,000 interactions for billion-scale recommendation platforms using asymmetric train-sparse infer-dense designs.
papers.link: This paper scales end-to-end user sequence processing to 10,000 interactions for industrial recommendation. UNIQUE operates in the same industrial feed domain, but focuses on replacing the multi-stage funnel with quantized generative retrieval and ranking.

papers.t: OneTrans: Unified Feature Interaction and Sequence Modeling with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender
papers.idea: Combines feature interaction and user sequence modeling into a single unified Transformer backbone processed in a per-token formulation.
papers.link: OneTrans integrates feature interactions and sequence modeling into a single Transformer backbone for industrial CTR prediction. UNIQUE goes beyond sequence-level ranking to unify candidate retrieval and ranking into a single quantized model.

papers.t: Sentence-T5: Scalable Sentence Encoders from Pre-trained Text-to-Text Models
papers.idea: Develops and benchmarks methods to extract dense sentence embeddings from pre-trained encoder-decoder T5 models.
papers.link: Sentence-T5 evaluates dense embedding extraction from encoder-decoder models for semantic text similarity. UNIQUE relies on generative code decoding and discriminative scoring over discrete items rather than continuous sentence embeddings.

papers.t: Natural Questions: A Benchmark for Question Answering Research
papers.idea: Presents a real-world question-answering benchmark consisting of actual Google search queries paired with Wikipedia evidence and answers.
papers.link: Natural Questions benchmarks open-domain question answering over real search queries and Wikipedia text. UNIQUE addresses industrial feed recommendation and evaluates on user interaction logs.

papers.t: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
papers.idea: Introduces the text-to-text transfer Transformer framework, converting every natural language processing task into a uniform sequence-to-sequence problem.
papers.link: T5 formulates disparate NLP tasks into a single sequence-to-sequence framework. UNIQUE applies this general philosophy to industrial recommenders, framing both candidate retrieval and scoring within an autoregressive discrete code architecture.

papers.t: Introducing Deep Research
papers.idea: Introduces an autonomous agent system designed to execute multi-step web search, document retrieval, and evidence synthesis for research tasks.
papers.link: Deep Research constructs multi-step browsing agents to gather and synthesize text evidence across the web. UNIQUE solves large-scale feed item recommendation, using quantized generative retrieval instead of open-ended search agents.

papers.t: Large Language Models Can Accurately Predict Searcher Preferences
papers.idea: Evaluates the capability of large language models to serve as zero-shot or few-shot judges for relevance and searcher preferences in information retrieval.
papers.link: This paper investigates language models as judges for evaluating search relevance. UNIQUE focuses on model architecture and training for live feed recommendation rather than LLM-based offline evaluation.

papers.t: LightRAG: Simple and Fast Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.idea: Introduces a dual-level knowledge graph structure to index corpora and enable both low-level and high-level entity and relationship retrieval for retrieval-augmented generation.
papers.link: LightRAG builds a two-level entity-relation graph for text retrieval in generative question answering. UNIQUE focuses on industrial recommendation, using discrete vector quantization of item embeddings instead of text knowledge graphs.

papers.t: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval
papers.idea: Constructs a recursive tree of text summaries through clustering to enable retrieval across multiple levels of abstraction in retrieval-augmented systems.
papers.link: RAPTOR organizes text summaries into hierarchical trees for multi-level text retrieval. In contrast, UNIQUE eliminates hierarchical tree structures in favor of flat single-layer quantization for item recommendation.

papers.t: OneRec Technical Report
papers.idea: Details the architecture, scaling metrics, and system deployment of an industrial generative recommendation framework unifying candidate generation and ranking.
papers.link: OneRec presents an industrial deployment of generative recommendation unifying retrieval and ranking with hierarchical semantic IDs. UNIQUE directly addresses OneRec's formulation, replacing its hierarchical IDs with flat quantization to avoid error propagation on long-tail items.

papers.t: KuaiRand: An Unbiased Sequential Recommendation Dataset with Randomly Exposed Videos
papers.idea: Releases an unbiased recommendation dataset containing long sequential user histories alongside randomly exposed video items to mitigate position and exposure bias.
papers.link: KuaiRand provides an unbiased evaluation dataset with randomly exposed videos for sequential recommender systems. UNIQUE focuses on the architecture side of sequential recommendation, unifying retrieval and ranking via quantization.

papers.t: Fine-Tuning LLaMA for Multi-Stage Text Retrieval
papers.idea: Presents a fine-tuning recipe to adapt decoder-only LLaMA models into dense bi-encoder text representations and rerankers for multi-stage retrieval pipelines.
papers.link: This paper adapts decoder-only LLaMA models for dense text retrieval and reranking. UNIQUE also uses a decoder backbone, but replaces the dual dense-retrieval and reranker pipeline with a unified generative and discriminative code architecture.

papers.t: Query2doc: Query Expansion with Large Language Models
papers.idea: Generates pseudo-documents from queries using large language models and combines them with original queries to improve sparse and dense first-stage retrieval.
papers.link: Query2doc uses large language models to generate synthetic text expansions for document search. UNIQUE addresses feed recommendation without text query expansion, instead predicting discrete item codes directly from user history.

papers.t: DeepFM: A Factorization-Machine based Neural Network for CTR Prediction
papers.idea: The authors integrate a factorization machine with a deep neural network into a single end-to-end architecture that shares raw input embeddings. The factorization machine component models explicit low-order feature interactions, while the deep network captures implicit high-order interactions without manual feature engineering.
papers.link: DeepFM serves as a foundational baseline for explicit and implicit feature interactions in ranking stages. UNIQUE moves beyond separate ranking models by unifying candidate retrieval and ranking into a single quantized network.

papers.t: Towards General Text Embeddings with Multi-stage Contrastive Learning
papers.idea: The paper presents the General Text Embedding (GTE) framework, which trains dense bi-encoders using a multi-stage contrastive learning pipeline. The process progresses from pre-training on large weakly supervised text pairs to fine-tuning on diverse retrieval tasks with hard negatives.
papers.link: GTE outlines multi-stage contrastive training for dense bi-encoder text representations. UNIQUE targets item recommendation, replacing dual-encoder dense retrieval with generative quantized code prediction.

papers.t: RankZephyr: Effective and robust zero-shot listwise reranking is a breeze!
papers.idea: The authors introduce a 7B-parameter open instruction-tuned language model tailored for zero-shot listwise document reranking. The model is trained via distillation from proprietary frontier language models that perform listwise sorting prompts.
papers.link: RankZephyr distills language models for zero-shot listwise document reranking. UNIQUE focuses on feed recommendation, combining candidate generation with point-level discriminative scoring in one framework.

papers.t: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
papers.idea: The paper analyzes sampled evaluation metrics where candidate items are drawn from a subset of non-interacted items rather than the entire catalog. It shows that sampled metrics frequently fail to preserve the true relative rankings of recommendation algorithms, advocating for full-catalog evaluation.
papers.link: This paper analyzes the evaluation risks of candidate sampling in top-K item recommendation. UNIQUE operates in the same item recommendation setting, deploying full-corpus generative retrieval across its catalog codes.

papers.t: Qwen3-VL-Embedding and Qwen3-VL-Reranker: A Unified Framework for State-of-the-Art Multimodal Retrieval and Ranking
papers.idea: The work presents a unified vision-language retrieval framework comprising an embedding bi-encoder for dense candidate generation and a cross-modal reranker for fine scoring. Both components leverage large vision-language foundation models trained across diverse multimodal text and image tasks.
papers.link: Qwen3-VL provides separate bi-encoder retrieval and cross-encoder reranking models for multimodal search. UNIQUE merges retrieval and ranking into a single unified architecture for user feed recommendation.

expeditions.name: From Token Routing to Autoregressive Item Prediction
expeditions.q: How did retrieval evolve from multi-stage cascading pipelines into single unified generative rankers?
expeditions.insight: Early systems separate candidate selection, pre-ranking, and click-through rate prediction into distinct operational blocks. Newer approaches unify these stages into shared transformer backbones that map long-horizon user histories to discrete semantic IDs. Single-step generation avoids autoregressive latency bottlenecks while preserving catalog coverage.

expeditions.name: The Shift from Dense Passages to Document Graphs
expeditions.q: How does passage retrieval bridge the gap toward multi-hop cross-document reasoning?
expeditions.insight: Bi-encoders and late-interaction systems effectively score individual text chunks but struggle with multi-hop dependencies. Integrating hierarchical graphs and topic hypergraphs allows models to trace evidence across isolated text islands. This structure enables calibrated abstention when cross-document evidence chains break.

expeditions.name: Establishing Generative Search Indexes
expeditions.q: Can learned neural memories completely replace inverted lists and vector index structures?
expeditions.insight: Replacing external vector libraries with sequence-to-sequence memory requires constructing hierarchical semantic identifiers via residual quantization. Early architectures suffered from linguistic forgetting and codebook collapse during index updates. Modern multi-resolution loss objectives and bottom-up clustering preserve language capabilities during dynamic corpus updates.

expeditions.name: Diagnosing LLM Evaluation Reliability
expeditions.q: How reliable are automated LLM judges when scoring search relevance and agentic answer quality?
expeditions.insight: LLM judges exhibit sensitivity to conversational prompt tone, inducing arbitrary operating-point shifts during evaluation. Further audits reveal that while models lack strong self-preference premiums, they frequently certify unsupported claims in complex multi-step tasks. Calibrating evaluator scores requires item response theory and strict receipt-level evidence verification.

open.t: How to prevent codebook collapse during dynamic corpus additions?
open.text: Continual generative indexing alters the assignment boundaries of existing items when new text enters the collection. Current systems lack online updating rules that prevent semantic drift without full retuning.

open.t: When does multimodal late interaction justify its memory overhead?
open.text: Stashing uncompressed vision-language embeddings for every document patch incurs substantial serving footprints. Researchers need strict criteria to determine which visual queries require multi-vector matching over single-vector projections.

open.t: How to prevent catastrophic hallucination in multi-hop graph retrieval?
open.text: Graph traversal components occasionally traverse noisy relational edges that stitch together incompatible facts. Reliable confidence estimators are needed to trigger abstention before passing corrupted contexts to generation backbones.

open.t: How to preserve prompt invariance in automated LLM relevance judges?
open.text: Evaluator severity fluctuates when users or prompts alter politeness levels and conversational style. Models require objective calibration mechanisms that decouple semantic relevance scoring from surface phrasing variations.

open.t: How to avoid hindsight leakage in evolving enterprise data lakes?
open.text: Static benchmark evaluation fails to capture temporal dependencies present in dynamic organizational tabular stores. Retrieval architectures must maintain point-in-time correctness without leaking future states into historical join paths.
